current projections span a range wide enough to make precise, decades-ahead planning genuinely difficult
Model projections of Thwaites' future remain strikingly divergent
if this buttressing effect were entirely lost, surrounding glaciers could eventually contribute an additional three metres of sea-level rise

bedrock that slopes downward inland, meaning that once retreat begins, warmer ocean water can flow ever deeper beneath the ice, accelerating melting rather than slowing it, a self-reinforcing process glaciologists call marine ice sheet instability

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "Had retreat not accelerated, sea levels would have risen slower."
"Scientists recommended that the team monitors the cavity closely."
"The number of research expeditions continue to grow yearly."
"Neither the sensors nor the ship were fully reliable."
"Having mapped the cavity, researchers revised their models."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "Had retreat not accelerated, sea levels would have risen slower."**

This is a third-conditional counterfactual with inverted Had + past participle ("Had retreat not accelerated") paired with "would have risen." The comparative adverb "slower" is acceptable exam English beside "more slowly" when comparing rates.

**Tip:** Inversion (Had + subject + past participle) is just another way to write If + past perfect.

The inverted third conditional is well formed, so the sentence stands.

**B) "Scientists recommended that the team monitors the cavity closely."**

After recommend + that, exam English wants the mandative subjunctive: base form monitor, not third-person monitors. The finite "monitors" treats the clause like an ordinary present indicative.

**Trap:** Recommend/insist/require + that → base verb, even with a singular subject.

The subjunctive needs "monitor," so this wording fails — "Scientists recommended that the team monitor the cavity closely."

**C) "The number of research expeditions continue to grow yearly."**

The head of the subject is "number," which is singular, so the verb should be continues. "Continue" wrongly agrees with the plural noun inside the of-phrase ("expeditions").

**Tip:** The number of → singular; a number of → plural.

Singular "number" needs "continues," so the line fails — "The number of research expeditions continues to grow yearly."

**D) "Neither the sensors nor the ship were fully reliable."**

Neither…nor joins a plural noun ("sensors") and a singular one ("ship"). In this bank's mixed-number reading, plural agreement is allowed because one member of the pair is plural, so "were" can stand.

**Tip:** When neither…nor mixes numbers, check which agreement rule the item expects—here the plural partner licenses "were."

With a plural noun in the neither…nor pair, "were" fits, so the sentence is sound.

**E) "Having mapped the cavity, researchers revised their models."**

The perfect participle "Having mapped" correctly sets mapping as earlier work by the same agents who then "revised"—researchers are both the mappers and the revisers, so there is no dangling modifier.

The participial opener attaches cleanly to "researchers," so the wording holds.

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "No sooner had radar scanned the ice than the cavity appeared."
"The programme, along with related studies, were funded jointly."
"Each of the models have projected differing timelines."
"By the time data arrives, projections will have already shifted."
"The readings, which were gathered yearly, show accelerating melt."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "No sooner had radar scanned the ice than the cavity appeared."**

No sooner + inverted past perfect ("had radar scanned") pairs with than + past simple ("appeared"). That is the classic No sooner…than pattern for a near-immediate follow-on event.

The inversion and than-clause are correctly built, so the sentence stands.

**B) "The programme, along with related studies, were funded jointly."**

The real subject is singular "programme"; the parenthetical "along with related studies" does not make the verb plural. Were should be was.

**Trap:** Along with / as well as / together with never turns a singular head into a plural subject.

Singular "programme" needs "was funded," so this fails — "The programme, along with related studies, was funded jointly."

**C) "Each of the models have projected differing timelines."**

Each of + plural noun still takes a singular verb: has projected, not have. "Each" points one-by-one and keeps the head singular.

"Each" demands singular "has," so the line fails — "Each of the models has projected differing timelines."

**D) "By the time data arrives, projections will have already shifted."**

"By the time" + present ("arrives") sets a future reference point; "will have already shifted" places that change before data arrives—future perfect for prior completion.

Completion before a future "by the time" moment is exactly future perfect's job, so the wording is sound.

**E) "The readings, which were gathered yearly, show accelerating melt."**

Plural "readings" correctly takes "were" in the non-restrictive relative clause and "show" in the main clause. Number agreement is consistent throughout.

Plural subject and plural verbs align, so the sentence holds.

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use.
statements: In Paragraph 2, "self-reinforcing" means weakening over repeated cycles.
In Paragraph 3, "eroding" means gradually wearing something away.
In Paragraph 4, "buttress" means something that supports and holds back.
In Paragraph 6, "hazardous" means completely safe and risk-free.
In Paragraph 9, "hidden" means fully visible and easily observed.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 2, "self-reinforcing" means weakening over repeated cycles.**

In Paragraph 2 the process accelerates melt rather than slowing it—the loop strengthens itself. "Weakening over repeated cycles" is the opposite polarity of a self-reinforcing feedback.

**Trap:** "Self-" compounds often tempt antonym glosses; here the ice-sheet loop intensifies, it does not fade.

Accelerating, not weakening, is the sense in Paragraph 2, so the gloss fails.

**B) In Paragraph 3, "eroding" means gradually wearing something away.**

Paragraph 3 says warm water was "reaching, and eroding, the glacier's underside"—progressive basal wear. "Gradually wearing something away" is exactly that geologic sense.

Gradual wear matches how Paragraph 3 uses "eroding," so the meaning holds.

**C) In Paragraph 4, "buttress" means something that supports and holds back.**

Paragraph 4 calls the ice shelf a "natural buttress" that "holds back a much larger mass of ice further inland." Support-plus-restraint is the role the sentence assigns.

Holding inland ice back is the buttress function named there, so the gloss is true.

**D) In Paragraph 6, "hazardous" means completely safe and risk-free.**

Paragraph 6 describes waters once "considered too hazardous to survey directly"—dangerous enough to avoid. "Completely safe and risk-free" is the antonym of that risk label.

Hazardous marks danger, not safety, so the claimed meaning fails.

**E) In Paragraph 9, "hidden" means fully visible and easily observed.**

Paragraph 9 closes on the ice sheet's "hidden underside"—material researchers still pursue because it is not in plain view. "Fully visible" reverses that sense.

Hidden means concealed, not visible, so the gloss is false.
highlights: a self-reinforcing process glaciologists call marine ice sheet instability
warm water was reaching, and eroding, the glacier's underside
Acting as a natural buttress, its ice shelf currently holds back a much larger mass of ice further inland
waters that had previously been considered too hazardous to survey directly
glaciologists studying the ice sheet's hidden underside

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use.
statements: In Paragraph 1, "disintegrate" means to break apart completely.
In Paragraph 5, "extrapolate" means to project forward from existing trends.
In Paragraph 7, "divergent" means closely matching one another.
In Paragraph 8, "genuinely" means falsely or only apparently.
In Paragraph 2, "accelerating" means slowing down gradually.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 1, "disintegrate" means to break apart completely.**

Paragraph 1 weighs what happens if Thwaites were to "disintegrate entirely"—total breakup releasing enough ice for a ~65 cm rise. "Break apart completely" tracks that total-collapse sense.

Entire breakup is how Paragraph 1 uses the verb, so the meaning holds.

**B) In Paragraph 5, "extrapolate" means to project forward from existing trends.**

Paragraph 5 says stop-start retreat complicates efforts "to extrapolate a single, simple future trajectory from past trends." That is textbook projecting-forward from known data.

Projecting a future path from past trends is exactly the Paragraph 5 sense, so the gloss is true.

**C) In Paragraph 7, "divergent" means closely matching one another.**

Paragraph 7's projections "remain strikingly divergent," with some runs on decades and others on centuries. "Closely matching" erases that split.

**Trap:** Do not gloss divergent as "aligned"; the paragraph's decades-versus-centuries contrast proves separation.

Divergent means differing, not matching, so the claim fails.

**D) In Paragraph 8, "genuinely" means falsely or only apparently.**

Paragraph 8 says planning is "genuinely difficult" because the projection range is wide—"genuinely" intensifies real difficulty, not fake or apparent difficulty.

Genuinely means truly, not falsely, so the gloss is false.

**E) In Paragraph 2, "accelerating" means slowing down gradually.**

Paragraph 2 says warmer water leads to "accelerating melting rather than slowing it." The text even pairs accelerating against slowing, so "slowing down gradually" is the denied opposite.

Accelerating is speeding melt, not slowing it, so the meaning fails.
highlights: were it to disintegrate entirely
complicating efforts to extrapolate a single, simple future trajectory from past trends

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: One sentence from the passage, followed by five short paraphrases. Decide if each preserves its meaning. Original: "Model projections of Thwaites' future remain strikingly divergent."
statements: Forecasts for the glacier's future differ sharply from one another.
Forecasts for the glacier's future agree closely with each other.
The glacier's future is no longer being modelled at all.
Predictions about the glacier's fate vary considerably between models.
Every model now predicts the exact same outcome confidently.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Forecasts for the glacier's future differ sharply from one another.**

The original line is "Model projections of Thwaites' future remain strikingly divergent." "Forecasts…differ sharply" preserves both the modelling topic and the strong-disagreement sense of "strikingly divergent."

Sharp difference between forecasts is a faithful paraphrase, so the line matches.

**B) Forecasts for the glacier's future agree closely with each other.**

"Agree closely" is the antonym of "strikingly divergent." The paraphrase reverses the original's core claim about model disagreement.

**Trap:** Synonym traps often flip divergent ↔ agree; reject any close-agreement rewrite.

Close agreement contradicts divergence, so this paraphrase fails.

**C) The glacier's future is no longer being modelled at all.**

The original asserts that model projections still exist and disagree; it never says modelling has stopped. "No longer being modelled" invents a cessation the sentence does not contain.

Abandoned modelling is not in the original, so the paraphrase fails.

**D) Predictions about the glacier's fate vary considerably between models.**

"Vary considerably between models" restates divergent projections without softening or reversing them. "Fate" and "predictions" stay within the same forecasting domain as "model projections…future."

Considerable between-model variation keeps the original meaning, so the paraphrase holds.

**E) Every model now predicts the exact same outcome confidently.**

Unanimous, confident sameness cancels "strikingly divergent." The paraphrase invents agreement and certainty the source line denies.

Identical confident outcomes reverse the original, so this paraphrase is false.

Model projections of Thwaites' future remain strikingly divergent
Model projections of Thwaites' future remain strikingly divergent

tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Below roughly 200 metres, sunlight has largely faded.
Around 76% of deep-dwelling animals can self-illuminate.
Bioluminescence evolved through a single shared pathway only.
Some organisms glow continuously rather than in flashes.
Firefly bioluminescence relies on one well-studied chemical pathway.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Below roughly 200 metres, sunlight has largely faded.**

Paragraph 1 opens with the same depth threshold: below roughly 200 metres, sunlight fades until the ocean becomes a realm of near-total darkness. "Has largely faded" is a fair paraphrase of that fade into the aphotic layer, not a stronger claim than the text allows.

**Tip:** When a statement recycles the passage's own depth figure, check the surrounding clause instead of inventing a new threshold.

Paragraph 1 names the 200-metre fade directly, so the claim matches the text.

**B) Around 76% of deep-dwelling animals can self-illuminate.**

The same paragraph estimates that as many as 76% of animals living below this depth can produce their own light. "Around 76%" and "self-illuminate" track that figure and the bioluminescence definition without changing the percentage.

**Tip:** Quantity items are true when the number is unchanged and the wording only softens "as many as" into "around."

The 76% self-light estimate in paragraph 1 supports the statement.

**C) Bioluminescence evolved through a single shared pathway only.**

Paragraph 1 contrasts land fireflies' single well-studied pathway with deep-sea organisms that evolved the glow independently on dozens of separate occasions. "A single shared pathway only" erases that repeated reinvention and flattens the trait into one origin story.

**Trap:** The firefly contrast can lure you into applying "one pathway" to the deep sea; the passage reserves that description for fireflies on land.

The claim fails because the text says the deep-sea glow arose "on dozens of separate occasions," not once.

**D) Some organisms glow continuously rather than in flashes.**

Paragraph 2 states that some organisms produce light continuously, creating a faint, steady glow, while others trigger sudden flashes. The statement picks the continuous side of that explicit contrast and does not deny that flashing also occurs.

Paragraph 2's continuous-glow option matches the claim.

**E) Firefly bioluminescence relies on one well-studied chemical pathway.**

Paragraph 1 says bioluminescent fireflies on land rely on a single well-studied chemical pathway. That is exactly the land-side contrast used before discussing deep-sea reinvention.

The firefly pathway line in paragraph 1 matches the statement.
highlights: Below roughly 200 metres, sunlight fades until the ocean becomes a realm of near-total darkness
as many as 76% of animals living below this depth are capable of producing their own light
evolved the ability to glow independently on dozens of separate occasions
Some organisms produce light continuously, creating a faint, steady glow
bioluminescent fireflies on land, which rely on a single well-studied chemical pathway

tasks.title: Task 2
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Luciferin reacts with oxygen using luciferase.
Anglerfish males permanently fuse to females' bodies.
Fused males remain fully independent of the female.
Squid release glowing mucus purely to attract prey.
The 2020 survey recorded over 350 distinct species.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Luciferin reacts with oxygen using luciferase.**

Paragraph 2 explains that luciferin reacts with oxygen in the presence of the enzyme luciferase. "Using luciferase" is ordinary shorthand for that enzyme-mediated reaction, not a new chemical story.

The luciferin–oxygen–luciferase description in paragraph 2 matches the claim.

**B) Anglerfish males permanently fuse to females' bodies.**

Paragraph 3 describes several species in which a much smaller male permanently fuses to the female's body, with tissues and circulatory systems merging. "Permanently fuse" repeats that reproductive attachment rather than a temporary pairing.

Paragraph 3's permanent-fusion account supports the statement.

**C) Fused males remain fully independent of the female.**

After fusion, the male becomes little more than an attached sperm-producing appendage, entirely dependent on the female's bloodstream. "Fully independent" reverses that dependence into its opposite.

**Trap:** Fusion language can sound like a partnership of equals; the passage ends on one-way dependence.

The claim fails because the male is "entirely dependent on the female's bloodstream for survival."

**D) Squid release glowing mucus purely to attract prey.**

Paragraph 4 says certain squid release clouds of glowing mucus or ink to startle and disorient predators, buying time to escape. Attraction of prey belongs to the anglerfish lure earlier; here the mucus is defensive, not a hunting bait, and "purely to attract prey" invents the wrong purpose.

The claim fails: glowing mucus is deployed "to startle and disorient predators," not to lure prey.

**E) The 2020 survey recorded over 350 distinct species.**

Paragraph 6 reports that a 2020 ROV survey recorded bioluminescent responses across more than 350 distinct species. "Over 350" faithfully restates "more than 350" without inflating the count.

The 2020 survey total in paragraph 6 matches the statement.
highlights: a light-emitting molecule called luciferin reacting with oxygen in the presence of an enzyme, luciferase
a much smaller male permanently fuses to the body of a female
entirely dependent on the female's bloodstream for survival
certain squid release clouds of glowing mucus or ink to startle and disorient predators
recorded bioluminescent responses across more than 350 distinct species

tasks.title: Task 3
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Counter-illumination erases a fish's downward-facing shadow.
Glowing species proportions declined sharply with depth.
Ostracods display species-specific courtship flash patterns.
The luciferin-luciferase reaction has no laboratory applications.
The 2020 survey extended to roughly 4,000 metres.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Counter-illumination erases a fish's downward-facing shadow.**

Paragraph 5 defines counter-illumination as a faint underside glow matching dim downwelling light, effectively erasing the shadow a body would cast when viewed from below. That is precisely the downward-silhouette problem the technique solves.

Paragraph 5's "erasing the shadow" wording matches the claim.

**B) Glowing species proportions declined sharply with depth.**

The 2020 survey found that the proportion of glowing species remained remarkably consistent across most of the depth range rather than declining steadily as researchers first expected. "Declined sharply" invents the trend the passage explicitly rejects.

**Trap:** Expectation of decline is mentioned only as the outdated hypothesis, not as the result.

The claim fails because the proportion "remained remarkably consistent … rather than declining steadily."

**C) Ostracods display species-specific courtship flash patterns.**

Paragraph 7 notes that researchers studying ostracods have documented complex, species-specific flash patterns used during courtship displays. The statement compresses that finding without adding a new claim about the unknown neurological mechanism.

The ostracod courtship line in paragraph 7 supports the statement.

**D) The luciferin-luciferase reaction has no laboratory applications.**

Paragraph 8 says the reaction has been adapted into a widely used laboratory tool for gene-expression markers and calls the technique genuinely indispensable in molecular biology and medical research. "No laboratory applications" flatly denies that lab career.

The claim fails: the passage calls the tool "genuinely indispensable across modern molecular biology and medical research."

**E) The 2020 survey extended to roughly 4,000 metres.**

Paragraph 6 places the encounters between the surface and roughly 4,000 metres depth. The statement simply restates that depth ceiling.

The survey's depth range in paragraph 6 matches the claim.
highlights: effectively erasing the shadow their bodies would otherwise cast when viewed from below
the proportion of glowing species remained remarkably consistent across most of that entire depth range rather than declining steadily
complex, species-specific flash patterns used during courtship displays
a technique that has become genuinely indispensable across modern molecular biology and medical research
between the surface and roughly 4,000 metres depth

tasks.title: Task 4
tasks.context: Statements test whether an inference is actually supported, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Independent evolution implies bioluminescence offers strong survival value.
If 76% of deep species glow, most remain fully dark.
The "burglar alarm" effect implies marked predators become targets.
Counter-illumination implies matching light helps avoid detection.
Fused anglerfish males imply females gain no reproductive benefit.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Independent evolution implies bioluminescence offers strong survival value.**

Paragraph 1 stresses that deep-sea organisms reinvented glow on dozens of separate occasions, calling it one of the most repeatedly reinvented traits in the animal kingdom. Traits that keep evolving independently under aphotic conditions are the textbook footprint of strong adaptive payoff, not a one-off fluke.

**Tip:** "Repeatedly reinvented" is the cue that the inference is about advantage, not about one shared gene.

Independent reinvention across lineages supports reading bioluminescence as strongly useful for survival.

**B) If 76% of deep species glow, most remain fully dark.**

"As many as 76%" glowing already identifies a clear majority of bioluminescent animals. Inferring that most remain fully dark flips the arithmetic: the non-glowing remainder is the minority.

**Trap:** 76% can be misread as a minority if you fixate on the incomplete quarter instead of the percentage itself.

The inference fails because a 76% glowing share means most do not remain fully dark.

**C) The "burglar alarm" effect implies marked predators become targets.**

Paragraph 4 describes crustaceans ejecting particles that stick to an attacker and mark it as a conspicuous target for larger secondary predators—the "burglar alarm" effect. The nickname itself encodes the marked-predator → next-predator chain.

The burglar-alarm description in paragraph 4 supports that marked predators become targets.

**D) Counter-illumination implies matching light helps avoid detection.**

By matching downwelling light and erasing the body's shadow against the brighter water above, counter-illumination stops predators from spotting silhouettes from below. Matching light is therefore a concealment tool, not a display.

Paragraph 5's silhouette-erasing logic supports the avoidance inference.

**E) Fused anglerfish males imply females gain no reproductive benefit.**

The fusion turns the male into a permanently attached sperm-producing appendage on the female. That arrangement secures continuous access to sperm for the female; saying she gains "no reproductive benefit" contradicts the whole point of the strategy.

**Trap:** "Appendage" and "dependent" describe the male's loss of independence, not a reproductive null for the female.

The inference fails because permanent attachment supplies ongoing fertilisation, a clear benefit to the female.
highlights: making it one of the most repeatedly reinvented traits in the animal kingdom
as many as 76% of animals living below this depth are capable of producing their own light
a conspicuous target for larger, secondary predators lurking nearby, a strategy researchers have nicknamed the "burglar alarm" effect
effectively erasing the shadow their bodies would otherwise cast when viewed from below by predators searching upward for silhouettes
the male becomes little more than a permanently attached sperm-producing appendage

tasks.title: Task 5
tasks.context: Statements require linking details across sections, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Independent evolution helps explain why chemical mechanisms vary between species.
The 350-species survey supports the point about consistent depth-wide glowing.
Defensive glowing and lure-based glowing serve identical evolutionary purposes.
Counter-illumination and lure-based hunting both directly cause visible light.
Laboratory use of luciferin shows deep-sea study benefits other fields.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Independent evolution helps explain why chemical mechanisms vary between species.**

Paragraph 1's dozens of independent origins sit next to paragraph 2's note that molecular details vary considerably between unrelated species. Separate evolutionary inventions naturally leave different luciferin–luciferase chemistries rather than one frozen pathway.

Linking independent origins to chemical variety is a fair cross-section synthesis of paragraphs 1 and 2.

**B) The 350-species survey supports the point about consistent depth-wide glowing.**

Paragraph 6's survey of more than 350 species is the evidence base for the finding that glowing-species proportions stayed remarkably consistent across depth. The headcount and the consistency claim are one result, not two unrelated facts.

The 350-species survey in paragraph 6 directly backs the depth-consistent glowing claim.

**C) Defensive glowing and lure-based glowing serve identical evolutionary purposes.**

Anglerfish dangle a glowing lure to attract prey (paragraph 3), while paragraph 4 opens by saying bioluminescence serves purposes well beyond luring prey and then details defensive mucus and burglar-alarm marking. Attracting food and deterring or tagging predators are different jobs.

**Trap:** Both uses emit light, so it is easy to collapse them into one "purpose"; the passage separates lure from defence.

The synthesis fails: defence and prey-luring are explicitly different functions.

**D) Counter-illumination and lure-based hunting both directly cause visible light.**

The anglerfish lure is a glowing bait, and counter-illumination produces a faint underside glow. Whatever their ends, both mechanisms emit visible light the animal can control or sustain.

Both strategies in paragraphs 3 and 5 produce visible light, so the shared-emission claim holds.

**E) Laboratory use of luciferin shows deep-sea study benefits other fields.**

Paragraph 8 moves from marine glow chemistry to a lab gene-expression marker that has become indispensable in molecular biology and medical research. That is the passage's own bridge from deep-sea chemistry to other sciences.

Paragraph 8's laboratory adaptation shows deep-sea bioluminescence feeding other fields.
highlights: the precise molecular details vary considerably between unrelated species
the proportion of glowing species remained remarkably consistent across most of that entire depth range
Bioluminescence serves purposes well beyond luring prey. Many species use it defensively
females dangle a glowing lure directly in front of their mouths to attract curious prey
The luciferinluciferase reaction has been adapted into a widely used laboratory tool

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "Had the survey not included deeper zones, fewer species would have been recorded."
"Researchers recommended that the team documents each flash pattern."
"The number of catalogued species continue to rise yearly."
"Neither the pressure nor the darkness were easily overcome."
"Having observed the pattern, scientists proposed a new hypothesis."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "Had the survey not included deeper zones, fewer species would have been recorded."**

This is inverted third conditional: Had + past participle stands in for If the survey had not …, and the result uses would have been recorded. The negative condition and past counterfactual result stay aligned.

**Tip:** Had + past participle at the front is a standard exam signal for inverted third conditionals.

The inversion and would-have result are sound, so the sentence is grammatically fine.

**B) "Researchers recommended that the team documents each flash pattern."**

After recommended that, formal English wants the subjunctive base form: document, not documents. The -s turns the clause into ordinary present and breaks the mandative pattern.

**Trap:** documents looks like ordinary third-person agreement after the team, which is exactly why the error hides.

The sentence fails; repair to "… that the team document each flash pattern."

**C) "The number of catalogued species continue to rise yearly."**

The grammatical subject is the number, which is singular, so the verb must be continues. Continue matches the plural species distractor instead of the head noun.

**Trap:** of catalogued species sits next to the verb and tempts plural agreement; ignore the of-phrase.

The sentence fails; repair to "The number of catalogued species continues to rise yearly."

**D) "Neither the pressure nor the darkness were easily overcome."**

With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. Darkness is singular, so the line needs was, not were. The extract's corrected key treats this as false for that proximity rule.

**Trap:** Neither … nor often feels "plural" because two things are named; exams still follow the nearer noun.

The sentence fails; repair to "Neither the pressure nor the darkness was easily overcome."

**E) "Having observed the pattern, scientists proposed a new hypothesis."**

The participle Having observed correctly attaches to scientists, the people who did the observing and then proposed the hypothesis. There is no dangling modifier onto an inanimate subject.

The participial opener matches its subject, so the sentence is grammatically fine.

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "No sooner had the vehicle descended than lights began flashing."
"The technique, along with related methods, were adopted widely."
"Each of the recorded species have shown distinct flash timing."
"By the time results arrive, models will have already changed."
"The samples, which were gathered over months, reveal consistent patterns."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "No sooner had the vehicle descended than lights began flashing."**

No sooner … than is a fixed inversion pattern: had + subject + past participle in the first clause, than introducing the second event. The timeline (descent, then flashing) is clean.

The no-sooner inversion is correctly formed, so the sentence is fine.

**B) "The technique, along with related methods, were adopted widely."**

The head subject is the technique (singular). The along with related methods phrase is parenthetical and does not make the subject plural, so were should be was.

**Trap:** related methods after the comma looks like a plural subject, but along with never joins subjects the way and does.

The sentence fails; repair to "The technique, along with related methods, was adopted widely."

**C) "Each of the recorded species have shown distinct flash timing."**

Each of takes a singular verb: has shown, not have shown. Species is the object of of, not the agreement controller.

**Trap:** species looks plural and sits beside the verb; each still forces singular.

The sentence fails; repair to "Each of the recorded species has shown distinct flash timing."

**D) "By the time results arrive, models will have already changed."**

By the time + present (arrive) pairs naturally with future perfect (will have already changed) for completion before a future reference point. The aspect fits a finished change ahead of the results' arrival.

Future perfect after by the time is the right frame, so the sentence is fine.

**E) "The samples, which were gathered over months, reveal consistent patterns."**

Samples is plural, so were in the relative clause and reveal in the main clause agree. The non-restrictive which-clause does not disturb the plural head.

Plural agreement holds throughout, so the sentence is fine.

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use.
statements: In Paragraph 1, "aphotic" means receiving abundant sunlight.
In Paragraph 3, "dangle" means to hang loosely, swinging.
In Paragraph 4, "conspicuous" means easily noticed or visible.
In Paragraph 5, "counterintuitively" means matching common expectations exactly.
In Paragraph 8, "indispensable" means unnecessary and easily removed.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 1, "aphotic" means receiving abundant sunlight.**

Paragraph 1 introduces the aphotic layer as the zone of near-total darkness after sunlight fades below roughly 200 metres. Aphotic labels the lightless realm, so "abundant sunlight" is the antonym of the context.

The claim fails: aphotic sits next to "near-total darkness," not abundant light.

**B) In Paragraph 3, "dangle" means to hang loosely, swinging.**

Female anglerfish dangle a glowing lure directly in front of their mouths. In that hunting scene, dangle is the familiar "hang loosely / suspend" sense, not a figurative stretch.

The lure sentence in paragraph 3 matches that hanging meaning.

**C) In Paragraph 4, "conspicuous" means easily noticed or visible.**

Particles stick to a predator and mark it as a conspicuous target for larger secondary predators. A target that must be easy for other hunters to spot is by definition easily noticed.

Paragraph 4's "conspicuous target" use matches "easily noticed or visible."

**D) In Paragraph 5, "counterintuitively" means matching common expectations exactly.**

The sentence begins "Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage"—light as hiding aid runs against the everyday expectation that light reveals. Matching expectations exactly would need intuitively, not counter-.

The claim fails: counterintuitively signals against expectation, not agreement with it.

**E) In Paragraph 8, "indispensable" means unnecessary and easily removed.**

The lab technique is called genuinely indispensable across molecular biology and medical research. Indispensable means essential; "unnecessary and easily removed" flips that into the opposite.

The claim fails: indispensable in paragraph 8 means the tool cannot be done without.
highlights: near-total darkness, a zone marine biologists call the aphotic layer
whose females dangle a glowing lure directly in front of their mouths
effectively marking that predator as a conspicuous target
Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage
a technique that has become genuinely indispensable across modern molecular biology and medical research

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use.
statements: In Paragraph 2, "deploying" means releasing or putting into use.
In Paragraph 6, "remarkably" means unremarkably or without any surprise.
In Paragraph 7, "documented" means recorded through careful observation.
In Paragraph 3, "fuses" means separates completely and permanently.
In Paragraph 9, "comprehensively" means only partially or incompletely.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 2, "deploying" means releasing or putting into use.**

Organisms trigger flashes, "deploying their light with a precision that suggests deliberate behavioural control." Deploying here is active use of the light tool, not merely possessing it.

Paragraph 2's controlled-flash wording matches "releasing or putting into use."

**B) In Paragraph 6, "remarkably" means unremarkably or without any surprise.**

The survey found proportions that "remained remarkably consistent," contrary to an initial expectation of decline. Remarkably heightens how notable that consistency is; "unremarkably" cancels the adverb.

The claim fails: remarkably marks surprise or note-worthiness, not the absence of surprise.

**C) In Paragraph 7, "documented" means recorded through careful observation.**

Researchers "have documented complex, species-specific flash patterns" in ostracods. Documented is the researcher's record of observed courtship flashes, not a casual rumour.

The ostracod line in paragraph 7 matches careful observational recording.

**D) In Paragraph 3, "fuses" means separates completely and permanently.**

The male permanently fuses to the female so tissues and circulatory systems merge. Fuse means join into one; "separates completely" is the antonym of that merger.

The claim fails: fuses describes joining, not permanent separation.

**E) In Paragraph 9, "comprehensively" means only partially or incompletely.**

Paragraph 9 asks whether the full diversity of mechanisms will ever be comprehensively catalogued—i.e., covered thoroughly. Partially / incompletely would undercut "comprehensive," not define it.

The claim fails: comprehensively means fully and thoroughly, not only in part.
highlights: deploying their light with a precision that suggests deliberate behavioural control
the proportion of glowing species remained remarkably consistent
have documented complex, species-specific flash patterns used during courtship displays
a much smaller male permanently fuses to the body of a female
Whether the full diversity of deep-sea bioluminescent mechanisms will ever be comprehensively catalogued

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: One sentence from the passage, followed by five short paraphrases. Decide if each preserves its meaning. Original: "Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage."
statements: Surprisingly, producing light can actually help an animal hide.
As expected, light always makes an animal easier to spot.
Unexpectedly, glowing can serve a concealment function instead.
Predictably, light exclusively reveals an animal's exact location.
Against expectation, emitting light can help conceal an animal.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Surprisingly, producing light can actually help an animal hide.**

The original says counterintuitively light can serve as camouflage. Surprisingly ≈ counterintuitively, and help an animal hide ≈ serve as camouflage, so both the surprise and the concealment keep pace.

The paraphrase preserves the unexpected hiding function of light.

**B) As expected, light always makes an animal easier to spot.**

As expected reverses counterintuitively, and easier to spot erases camouflage. The line restores the default "light reveals" intuition the original overturns.

**Trap:** Easier to spot feels like common sense about light, which is exactly what the original calls counterintuitive.

The paraphrase flips both the stance and the function, so it does not match.

**C) Unexpectedly, glowing can serve a concealment function instead.**

Unexpectedly tracks counterintuitively, and concealment function instead restates camouflage as an alternate use of glow. Wording changes, meaning holds.

The paraphrase keeps the surprise-plus-concealment core of the original.

**D) Predictably, light exclusively reveals an animal's exact location.**

Predictably and exclusively reveals invert the original on two axes: stance (surprise → predictability) and function (camouflage → pure revelation). Nothing of the camouflage concession survives.

The paraphrase reverses the original, so it fails as a restatement.

**E) Against expectation, emitting light can help conceal an animal.**

Against expectation restates counterintuitively; emitting light … help conceal maps onto light as camouflage. Both hinge ideas remain.

The paraphrase matches the original's unexpected concealment claim.
highlights: Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage
Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage
Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage
Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage
Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage

tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Octopuses possess roughly 500 million neurons total.
Most neurons are concentrated inside the central brain.
About two-thirds of neurons reside within the arms.
A severed arm can briefly continue grasping food.
Arm behaviour always requires central brain control.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Octopuses possess roughly 500 million neurons total.**

Paragraph (1) opens with the exact scale of octopus neural hardware: roughly 500 million neurons, a count compared to that of some small mammals. The statement simply restates that total figure; nothing in the sentence invents a different number or a different animal.

**Tip:** When a claim recycles a named quantity from the first sentence of a paragraph, the matching span is almost always the proof.

The neuron total matches the passage figure, so the claim is true.

**B) Most neurons are concentrated inside the central brain.**

Paragraph (1) contrasts octopus organisation with vertebrates: rather than concentrating computational power in a single centralised brain, about two-thirds of the neurons sit in the arms. Saying "most" live in the central brain flips that architecture.

**Trap:** "Comparable to mammals" can tempt you toward a mammal-style brain story; the text rejects that layout.

The claim reverses the passage's distributed layout, so it fails.

**C) About two-thirds of neurons reside within the arms.**

The same opening paragraph states that approximately two-thirds of an octopus's neurons reside within its eight arms, which is exactly what "about two-thirds… within the arms" paraphrases. The wording is faithful to both the proportion and the location.

That proportion is stated outright in paragraph (1), so the statement holds.

**D) A severed arm can briefly continue grasping food.**

Paragraph (2) describes an amputated arm that, still linked to its local neural cluster, can keep reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation. "Severed" and "amputated" name the same event; "briefly" mirrors "for a brief period."

The severed-arm behaviour is described in those terms, so the claim matches the passage.

**E) Arm behaviour always requires central brain control.**

Paragraph (2) draws the opposite lesson: the amputated-arm episode suggests that at least some goal-directed behaviour does not strictly require centralised, brain-level control. The absolute "always" collapses that nuance into a universal rule the text denies.

**Trap:** Extreme words like always / never often fail when the text offers even one counterexample.

The passage says some arm behaviour need not depend on the central brain, so the absolute claim fails.
highlights: Octopuses possess roughly 500 million neurons, a number comparable to that of some small mammals
Rather than concentrating computational power inside a single centralised brain, approximately two-thirds of an octopus's neurons reside within its eight arms
approximately two-thirds of an octopus's neurons reside within its eight arms themselves
an amputated octopus arm, still connected to its own local neural cluster, can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body
at least some forms of goal-directed behaviour do not strictly require centralised, brain-level control at all

tasks.title: Task 2
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Chromatophores are controlled via slow hormonal signalling.
Colour shifts can occur within roughly 200 milliseconds.
Iridophores help produce effects pigment alone cannot.
Octopus skin becomes physically rough during texture mimicry.
Octopuses possess multiple types of colour photoreceptors.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Chromatophores are controlled via slow hormonal signalling.**

Paragraph (3) says specialised skin cells called chromatophores are controlled directly by the nervous system rather than through slower hormonal signalling. The statement swaps the actual control route for the slower pathway the text explicitly rejects.

**Trap:** The phrase "slower hormonal signalling" appears in the text as a contrast, not as the mechanism in use.

Nervous-system control, not hormonal signalling, is what the passage names, so the claim fails.

**B) Colour shifts can occur within roughly 200 milliseconds.**

The same camouflage paragraph states that an octopus can shift its skin colour and pattern within roughly 200 milliseconds — faster than a human blink. The statement lifts that timing figure without exaggeration.

The 200-millisecond figure is stated directly, so the claim is true.

**C) Iridophores help produce effects pigment alone cannot.**

Paragraph (4) places iridophores and leucophores beneath the chromatophores and says they manipulate light reflection and scattering to produce effects chromatophore pigment alone cannot achieve. Credit to iridophores for those extra optical effects follows the text.

Iridophores are named for precisely that role, so the statement holds.

**D) Octopus skin becomes physically rough during texture mimicry.**

Paragraph (4) stresses that the animal can imitate coarse, rocky texture while its actual skin remains physically smooth throughout the transformation. Physical roughness of the skin is exactly what the passage rules out.

**Trap:** Visual texture mimicry is not the same as a change in skin surface geometry.

The skin stays smooth, so the roughness claim fails.

**E) Octopuses possess multiple types of colour photoreceptors.**

Paragraph (5) opens by calling octopuses colour-blind and stating they possess only a single type of photoreceptor, unlike colour-sighted animals that rely on multiple types. "Multiple types" is the vertebrate contrast, not the octopus fact.

Only one photoreceptor type is attributed to octopuses, so the claim fails.
highlights: controlled directly by the nervous system rather than through slower hormonal signalling
shift its skin colour and pattern within roughly 200 milliseconds, faster than the blink of a human eye
manipulate light reflection and scattering to produce effects chromatophore pigment alone cannot achieve
despite the animal's actual skin remaining physically smooth throughout the transformation
possessing only a single type of photoreceptor rather than the multiple types most colour-sighted animals rely on

tasks.title: Task 3
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Octopuses have unscrewed jar lids for food.
Most octopus species live for several decades.
Females typically die shortly after eggs hatch.
Octopuses diverged from vertebrates roughly 500 million years ago.
Their nervous system shares direct inherited vertebrate ancestry.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Octopuses have unscrewed jar lids for food.**

Paragraph (6) lists laboratory feats that include several octopuses recorded unscrewing jar lids to reach food sealed inside. The statement is a clean paraphrase of that documented behaviour.

Jar-lid opening for food is explicitly recorded, so the claim matches the passage.

**B) Most octopus species live for several decades.**

Paragraph (7) says most octopus species live for only one to two years — an unusually short lifespan. "Several decades" stretches that window by orders of magnitude and contradicts the stated range.

**Trap:** Impressive cognition can make a long lifespan feel "natural"; the numbers say otherwise.

One-to-two-year lives overturn the decades claim, so it fails.

**C) Females typically die shortly after eggs hatch.**

The same lifespan paragraph states that females typically die shortly after their eggs hatch, after stopping eating during a prolonged brooding period. The statement tracks that typical pattern.

Female mortality after hatching is stated directly, so the claim holds.

**D) Octopuses diverged from vertebrates roughly 500 million years ago.**

Paragraph (8) places the evolutionary split: octopuses diverged from the lineage leading to vertebrates roughly 500 million years ago. The quantity and the comparator lineage are both intact in the paraphrase.

The half-billion-year divergence figure is in the text, so the statement is true.

**E) Their nervous system shares direct inherited vertebrate ancestry.**

Paragraph (8) calls the octopus nervous system a product of convergent evolution entirely independent from the vertebrate brain pathway, "rather than a shared inherited trait." Claiming direct inherited vertebrate ancestry is the model the text rejects.

Independence via convergent evolution overturns shared ancestry, so the claim fails.
highlights: Several octopuses have been recorded unscrewing jar lids to reach food sealed inside
most octopus species live for only one to two years, an unusually short lifespan
Females typically die shortly after their eggs hatch, having stopped eating entirely during a prolonged brooding period
octopuses diverged from the lineage leading to vertebrates roughly 500 million years ago
a product of convergent evolution entirely independent from the evolutionary pathway that produced vertebrate brains, rather than a shared inherited trait

tasks.title: Task 4
tasks.context: Statements test whether an inference is actually supported, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Distributed neurons imply arms can act somewhat independently.
If arms hold two-thirds of neurons, one-third remains elsewhere.
Colour-blindness implies precise camouflage cannot possibly occur.
Short lifespan implies cognitive sophistication requires long-term learning.
Convergent evolution implies similar traits arose separately, not shared.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Distributed neurons imply arms can act somewhat independently.**

Paragraph (1) explains that putting roughly two-thirds of the neurons in the arms lets each arm process sensory information and initiate movement with a surprising degree of independence from the central brain. Paragraph (2) then shows severed-arm grasping that does not require brain-level control. The inference follows those facts rather than leaping past them.

Arm-level independence is the direct implication of the distributed layout, so the claim holds.

**B) If arms hold two-thirds of neurons, one-third remains elsewhere.**

Paragraph (1) assigns approximately two-thirds of the neurons to the arms. Arithmetic closes the rest: the remaining one-third must sit outside the arms — chiefly in the central nervous system the paragraph contrasts with. The inference adds no new biological claim beyond that split.

**Tip:** When the text gives a clean fraction, the complementary fraction is usually fair game if nothing else relocates those neurons.

Two-thirds in the arms leaves one-third elsewhere, so the statement is sound.

**C) Colour-blindness implies precise camouflage cannot possibly occur.**

Paragraph (5) acknowledges colour-blindness and then discusses how octopuses still achieve camouflage precisely matched to surrounding colouration, including a skin-photoreceptor hypothesis. Colour-blindness raises a puzzle; it does not license the absolute "cannot possibly occur."

**Trap:** A genuine research puzzle is not proof of impossibility.

Precise camouflage is described as real despite colour-blindness, so the impossibility claim fails.

**D) Short lifespan implies cognitive sophistication requires long-term learning.**

Paragraph (7) finds sophisticated behaviour especially puzzling given one-to-two-year lives — the short span is a tension with sophistication, not evidence that sophistication must rest on long-term learning. The "requires" leap is the reader's invention.

Short lifespan makes sophistication surprising rather than dependent on long learning, so the inference fails.

**E) Convergent evolution implies similar traits arose separately, not shared.**

Paragraph (8) defines the octopus case as convergent evolution entirely independent of the vertebrate pathway, not a shared inherited trait refined separately. That is exactly what "arose separately, not shared" means in this context.

The passage's own contrast equates convergent evolution with separate origin, so the claim holds.
highlights: allowing each arm to process sensory information and initiate movement with a surprising degree of independence from the central brain
approximately two-thirds of an octopus's neurons reside within its eight arms themselves
researchers have long debated how they achieve camouflage so precisely matched to their surroundings' actual colouration
Such capabilities appear especially puzzling given that most octopus species live for only one to two years
a product of convergent evolution entirely independent from the evolutionary pathway that produced vertebrate brains, rather than a shared inherited trait

tasks.title: Task 5
tasks.context: Statements require linking details across sections, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Distributed neurons help explain arm-level independent behaviour.
Colour-blindness and skin photoreceptors together suggest indirect colour sensing.
Short lifespan makes complex jar-opening behaviour easier to expect.
Convergent evolution helps explain why the nervous system differs from vertebrates.
Chromatophore speed and camouflage precision are entirely unrelated topics.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Distributed neurons help explain arm-level independent behaviour.**

Link paragraph (1)'s arm-resident neurons and local processing with paragraph (2)'s amputated-arm grasping: the distributed architecture is offered precisely as the reason arms can act with surprising independence. The synthesis stays inside what those sections supply.

Distributed neurons are the mechanism the text uses for arm independence, so the claim holds.

**B) Colour-blindness and skin photoreceptors together suggest indirect colour sensing.**

Paragraph (5) pairs colour-blindness (one photoreceptor type) with the still-unconfirmed idea that specialised skin photoreceptors let the animal sense colour indirectly through the skin, independent of the eyes. Reading those two details together is how the hypothesis is framed.

**Tip:** "Suggest" is the right verb here — the text calls the idea influential but not conclusively confirmed.

Colour-blindness plus skin photoreceptors underwrite the indirect-sensing hypothesis, so the statement is true.

**C) Short lifespan makes complex jar-opening behaviour easier to expect.**

Paragraph (6) presents jar-opening and related feats as cognitive achievements hard to square with a simple nervous system; paragraph (7) then calls such capabilities especially puzzling given the one-to-two-year lifespan. Short life makes the behaviour harder to expect, not easier.

**Trap:** Do not reverse the evaluative force of "puzzling."

The short lifespan deepens the puzzle rather than easing expectations, so the claim fails.

**D) Convergent evolution helps explain why the nervous system differs from vertebrates.**

Paragraph (1) establishes a layout "strikingly unlike" vertebrates; paragraph (8) explains that difference as convergent evolution on an independent pathway rather than shared inheritance. Convergent evolution is the evolutionary account of the structural difference.

Independent convergent origins account for the unlike architecture, so the synthesis holds.

**E) Chromatophore speed and camouflage precision are entirely unrelated topics.**

Paragraphs (3)–(5) form one camouflage thread: rapid chromatophore shifts, deeper iridophore/leucophore effects, and the puzzle of precise colour matching despite colour-blindness. Speed and precision belong to the same capability story, not to disconnected chapters.

They sit inside one camouflage discussion, so "entirely unrelated" fails.
highlights: approximately two-thirds of an octopus's neurons reside within its eight arms themselves, allowing each arm to process sensory information and initiate movement with a surprising degree of independence from the central brain
specialised photoreceptors distributed across the animal's own skin allow it to sense colour indirectly through the skin itself, entirely independent of its eyes

Such capabilities appear especially puzzling given that most octopus species live for only one to two years, an unusually short lifespan for an animal displaying this degree of behavioural sophistication
making their sophisticated nervous system a product of convergent evolution entirely independent from the evolutionary pathway that produced vertebrate brains

Specialised skin cells called chromatophores, controlled directly by the nervous system rather than through slower hormonal signalling, allow an octopus to shift its skin colour and pattern within roughly 200 milliseconds

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "Had the arm not been severed, it would have remained attached."
"Researchers recommended that the lab documents each behaviour."
"The number of recorded cases continue to grow."
"Neither the pigment nor the reflection were fully understood."
"Having observed the pattern, scientists proposed a new theory."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "Had the arm not been severed, it would have remained attached."**

This is a third-conditional counterfactual with inversion: Had + past participle opens the if-clause, and would have + past participle carries the unreal past result. The negative not been severed pairs cleanly with the hypothetical remaining attached.

**Tip:** Inversion with Had is a formal stand-in for If the arm had not been severed…

The inverted third conditional is well formed, so the sentence stands.

**B) "Researchers recommended that the lab documents each behaviour."**

After recommend that, English expects the mandative subjunctive: a bare base verb. Documents is present indicative agreement with lab, so the line should read that the lab document each behaviour.

**Trap:** Ordinary third-person -s feels natural after a singular subject, but recommend that blocks that pattern.

The subjunctive needs document, not documents, so the wording fails — "Researchers recommended that the lab document each behaviour."

**C) "The number of recorded cases continue to grow."**

The grammatical subject is the number, which is singular; of recorded cases is only a prepositional phrase. A singular subject needs continues, not the plural continue.

**Tip:** Contrast the number of (singular verb) with a number of (usually plural verb).

Singular the number cannot take continue, so the line fails — "The number of recorded cases continues to grow."

**D) "Neither the pigment nor the reflection were fully understood."**

With neither…nor, the verb typically agrees with the nearer subject. Reflection is singular, so were should be was: Neither the pigment nor the reflection was fully understood.

Proximity agreement picks singular was after reflection, so the wording does not hold — "Neither the pigment nor the reflection was fully understood."

**E) "Having observed the pattern, scientists proposed a new theory."**

The participle Having observed the pattern correctly attaches to scientists, the subject who did the observing and then proposed the theory. There is no dangling modifier or subject mismatch.

The participial opener belongs to scientists, so the sentence is sound.

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "No sooner had the lid loosened than the octopus reached inside."
"The study, along with related trials, were published together."
"Each of the tested octopuses have solved the maze."
"By the time results arrive, theories will have already shifted."
"The samples, which were gathered carefully, reveal consistent behaviour."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "No sooner had the lid loosened than the octopus reached inside."**

No sooner…than requires inversion in the first clause: No sooner had + subject + past participle, then than + the following event. Here had the lid loosened pairs correctly with than the octopus reached inside.

**Tip:** Prefer than (not when) after no sooner.

The No sooner…than inversion is correct, so the sentence stands.

**B) "The study, along with related trials, were published together."**

The head noun is the study; along with related trials is a parenthetical add-on and does not make the subject plural. The verb must be was published, not were published.

**Trap:** Material after along with / as well as / together with often tricks the ear into a plural verb.

Singular study needs was, so the wording fails — "The study, along with related trials, was published together."

**C) "Each of the tested octopuses have solved the maze."**

Each of takes a singular verb even when a plural noun follows of. Have solved should be has solved: Each of the tested octopuses has solved the maze.

Each demands singular has, so the line does not hold — "Each of the tested octopuses has solved the maze."

**D) "By the time results arrive, theories will have already shifted."**

By the time + present-time clause points to a future milestone; will have shifted is future perfect, placing the theories' change before that arrival. The tense pairing matches the deadline logic.

Future perfect correctly finishes the change before the later point, so the sentence is sound.

**E) "The samples, which were gathered carefully, reveal consistent behaviour."**

Samples is plural, so the non-restrictive which clause rightly uses were, and the main verb reveal stays plural. Agreement is consistent from relative clause through the main clause.

Plural samples are matched by were and reveal, so the wording holds.

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use.
statements: In Paragraph 1, "centralised" means gathered into one main location.
In Paragraph 3, "specialised" means generic and unremarkable.
In Paragraph 5, "indirectly" means through a direct, immediate route.
In Paragraph 6, "reflexive" means automatic and unthinking.
In Paragraph 8, "convergent" means arising from a shared ancestor.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 1, "centralised" means gathered into one main location.**

Paragraph (1) contrasts concentrating computational power inside a single centralised brain with the octopus's distributed arm neurons. In that contrast, centralised means gathered into one main location rather than spread across the arms.

The surrounding "single…brain" contrast supports that sense, so the meaning claim is true.

**B) In Paragraph 3, "specialised" means generic and unremarkable.**

Paragraph (3) calls chromatophores specialised skin cells devoted to rapid colour and pattern change. Specialised here means adapted for a particular function; "generic and unremarkable" is the opposite of that context.

**Trap:** Do not invent a plain-English antonym when the cell name itself signals a dedicated role.

The word marks purpose-built cells, not bland ones, so the gloss fails.

**C) In Paragraph 5, "indirectly" means through a direct, immediate route.**

Paragraph (5) proposes that skin photoreceptors let the octopus sense colour indirectly through the skin, entirely independent of its eyes. Indirectly means through a non-eye, roundabout route — not a direct, immediate one.

The claimed gloss reverses the adverb, so the meaning claim fails.

**D) In Paragraph 6, "reflexive" means automatic and unthinking.**

Paragraph (6) says cognitive feats are difficult to reconcile with a simple, reflexive nervous system. Paired with simple, reflexive points to automatic, unthinking responses — the foil for jar-opening and maze skill.

That contrast locks in the automatic sense, so the gloss holds.

**E) In Paragraph 8, "convergent" means arising from a shared ancestor.**

Paragraph (8) contrasts convergent evolution with "a shared inherited trait": the octopus pathway is independent of vertebrates. Convergent here means similar traits arising separately, not from a shared ancestor.

**Trap:** "Convergent" sounds like "coming together," but here it opposes shared ancestry.

The passage denies shared inheritance, so that gloss fails.
highlights: Rather than concentrating computational power inside a single centralised brain
Specialised skin cells called chromatophores, controlled directly by the nervous system rather than through slower hormonal signalling
allow it to sense colour indirectly through the skin itself, entirely independent of its eyes
difficult to reconcile with a simple, reflexive nervous system
a product of convergent evolution entirely independent from the evolutionary pathway that produced vertebrate brains, rather than a shared inherited trait

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use.
statements: In Paragraph 2, "amputated" means surgically or accidentally removed.
In Paragraph 4, "manipulate" means to skilfully influence or control.
In Paragraph 6, "reconcile" means to make consistent or compatible.
In Paragraph 7, "brooding" means actively hunting for new prey.
In Paragraph 9, "illuminate" means to make clearer or better understood.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 2, "amputated" means surgically or accidentally removed.**

Paragraph (2) discusses an amputated octopus arm continuing to reach and grasp after separation from the body. In that scene, amputated means the arm has been removed — whether by surgery or accident is secondary to the detachment itself.

Removal/separation is exactly what the context requires, so the gloss is true.

**B) In Paragraph 4, "manipulate" means to skilfully influence or control.**

Iridophores and leucophores "manipulate light reflection and scattering" to create effects pigment alone cannot achieve. That is skilful optical control of light, not social trickery.

The light-control reading fits the optical layering, so the meaning holds.

**C) In Paragraph 6, "reconcile" means to make consistent or compatible.**

The cognitive feats are "difficult to reconcile with a simple, reflexive nervous system" — hard to make those behaviours fit, or sit consistently with, a purely reflexive model. That is the "make compatible" sense.

Compatibility with a simple model is what the phrase questions, so the gloss is sound.

**D) In Paragraph 7, "brooding" means actively hunting for new prey.**

Paragraph (7) describes a prolonged brooding period during which females stop eating entirely until eggs hatch. Brooding here is egg-guarding, not hunting; the fasting undercuts any "actively hunting" reading.

**Trap:** Everyday "brooding" (moodiness) and biological brooding (egg care) are both unlike hunting.

Egg-tending, not prey-hunting, is the sense in use, so the gloss fails.

**E) In Paragraph 9, "illuminate" means to make clearer or better understood.**

Paragraph (9) asks whether studying octopus cognition will "meaningfully illuminate general principles" of how intelligence can arise. Illuminate here is figurative clarification — making principles clearer — not physical lighting.

Making general principles better understood matches the debate frame, so the claim holds.
highlights: an amputated octopus arm, still connected to its own local neural cluster, can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body
which manipulate light reflection and scattering to produce effects chromatophore pigment alone cannot achieve
cognitive feats difficult to reconcile with a simple, reflexive nervous system
having stopped eating entirely during a prolonged brooding period that can last several months
Whether studying octopus cognition will meaningfully illuminate general principles of how intelligence can arise

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: One sentence from the passage, followed by five short paraphrases. Decide if each preserves its meaning. Original: "An amputated octopus arm can continue reaching toward and grasping food."
statements: A severed arm can still reach for and grab food.
A severed arm immediately stops moving entirely.
A detached arm remains capable of grasping food briefly.
An intact, attached arm can reach toward food normally.
A removed arm continues performing food-directed movements.
tactical_explanations:
**A) A severed arm can still reach for and grab food.**

The original says an amputated octopus arm can continue reaching toward and grasping food. Severed ≈ amputated, reach for ≈ reaching toward, and grab ≈ grasping; the paraphrase keeps the same actor and action.

Same arm, same food-directed reaching, so the paraphrase preserves the meaning.

**B) A severed arm immediately stops moving entirely.**

The source claim is continued reaching and grasping after amputation, not total stillness. "Immediately stops moving entirely" reverses both the motion and the brief persistence of the behaviour.

**Trap:** Absolute stop language is the near-miss false when the text stresses continuation.

Continued grasping overturns total cessation, so this paraphrase fails.

**C) A detached arm remains capable of grasping food briefly.**

Detached matches amputated/separated, grasping food matches the original action, and briefly reflects paragraph (2)'s "for a brief period." The paraphrase stays faithful while importing that short-duration cue from the same sentence.

Capability plus brief duration both track the passage, so the meaning holds.

**D) An intact, attached arm can reach toward food normally.**

The original is about an amputated arm after separation. Shifting to an intact, attached arm quietly changes the subject and drops the surprising post-separation behaviour the sentence exists to report.

**Trap:** A bland true-sounding fact about normal arms is still a wrong paraphrase of this line.

The intact-arm rewrite abandons the amputated subject, so it does not preserve the meaning.

**E) A removed arm continues performing food-directed movements.**

Removed restates amputated, and "continues performing food-directed movements" compresses "continue reaching toward and grasping food" without adding or contradicting content.

Removal plus continued food-directed motion match the original, so the paraphrase stands.
highlights: an amputated octopus arm, still connected to its own local neural cluster, can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body
can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body
can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body
an amputated octopus arm, still connected to its own local neural cluster, can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body
