tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included and increased vocabulary precision.
statements: The three-sector model's originators framed structural transformation as a near-universal consequence of rising income, not mere coincidence.
South Korea's structural transformation is described as having taken considerably longer than comparable European transitions.
Deindustrialization is described as occurring exclusively where manufacturing output genuinely contracts.
US manufacturing's employment share fell below 9% even as real output roughly tripled.
The quaternary sector proposal treats codified, specialised knowledge as analytically indispensable to its distinction from tertiary services.
tactical_explanations:
**A) The three-sector model's originators framed structural transformation as a near-universal consequence of rising income, not mere coincidence.**

Paragraph 1 says the originators framed the trajectory as "a near-universal consequence of rising income and shifting consumer demand rather than a mere historical coincidence." The statement restates that causal framing faithfully — rising income drives the shift; coincidence is rejected.

**Tip:** Match the exact framing words (near-universal, rising income, coincidence) before you decide.

The claim tracks Paragraph 1's wording, so it is true.

**B) South Korea's structural transformation is described as having taken considerably longer than comparable European transitions.**

Paragraph 1 calls Korea's change "a compression of structural transformation that took many earlier-industrialising European economies well over a century to accomplish." Compressed means shorter, not longer — the trap flips the comparison.

**Trap:** Chronology flip — "longer" reverses what "compression" means.

The statement reverses the passage's time comparison, so it fails.

**C) Deindustrialization is described as occurring exclusively where manufacturing output genuinely contracts.**

Paragraph 2 says deindustrialization draws scrutiny "precisely because it appears to unfold even where manufacturing itself remains robust rather than genuinely contracting." "Exclusively where…contracts" is the opposite of that point.

**Trap:** Absolute "exclusively" ignores the robust-output case the text stresses.

The claim invents a contraction-only rule the passage rejects, so it is false.

**D) US manufacturing's employment share fell below 9% even as real output roughly tripled.**

Paragraph 2 gives both figures together: employment share fell "to under 9% by 2020, even as manufacturing output, adjusted for inflation, roughly tripled." The statement pairs those facts without twisting either one.

The numeric pairing matches Paragraph 2 exactly, so the claim holds.

**E) The quaternary sector proposal treats codified, specialised knowledge as analytically indispensable to its distinction from tertiary services.**

Paragraph 3 contrasts information-intensive work with routine tertiary services by "heavy reliance on specialised, codified knowledge," and calls that distinction "analytically indispensable." The statement captures both the knowledge criterion and its analytical weight.

The proposal's own rationale supports the claim, so it is true.
highlights: framed as a near-universal consequence of rising income and shifting consumer demand rather than a mere historical coincidence
a compression of structural transformation that took many earlier-industrialising European economies well over a century to accomplish
even where manufacturing itself remains robust rather than genuinely contracting
fell from around 24% in 1970 to under 9% by 2020, even as manufacturing output, adjusted for inflation, roughly tripled
a distinction proponents consider analytically indispensable

tasks.title: Task 2
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Quinary sector boundaries are described as consistently tracked as a separate category by all national statistical agencies.
The 2018 study's divergence pattern is described as a mere artefact of US-specific statistical conventions.
Manufacturing value added grew in 33 of the 38 economies where employment share had declined.
The Sub-Saharan African employment-GDP gap is attributed mainly to inherent, unchangeable limitations of agriculture itself.
Underinvestment in technology and infrastructure is cited as a contributing factor to low agricultural output per worker.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Quinary sector boundaries are described as consistently tracked as a separate category by all national statistical agencies.**

Paragraph 4 says boundaries "remain genuinely contested and are applied inconsistently," with some agencies folding quinary activities "directly back into broader tertiary or quaternary categories." "Consistently…by all" invents uniformity the text denies.

**Trap:** "All…consistently" overstates what contested, inconsistent practice allows.

The claim fails because agencies do not track quinary as one neat separate category.

**B) The 2018 study's divergence pattern is described as a mere artefact of US-specific statistical conventions.**

Paragraph 5 opens by saying the US employment–output divergence "is by no means unique to it, nor is it merely an artefact of one country's particular statistical conventions," then cites the 42-economy study. Calling the pattern a US-only artefact reverses that framing.

The passage explicitly rejects the artefact reading, so the statement is false.

**C) Manufacturing value added grew in 33 of the 38 economies where employment share had declined.**

Paragraph 5 reports employment share declining in 38 economies, while "manufacturing value added…nonetheless grew in 33 of those same 38 economies." The statement repeats that nested count accurately.

The 33-of-38 figure matches the study summary, so the claim is true.

**D) The Sub-Saharan African employment-GDP gap is attributed mainly to inherent, unchangeable limitations of agriculture itself.**

Paragraph 6 attributes the gap to lower output per worker from "persistent underinvestment in agricultural technology, infrastructure, and access to capital rather than any inherent limitation of the sector itself." "Inherent, unchangeable" is exactly what the text rules out.

**Trap:** The word "inherent" appears — but only inside a rejection.

The statement flips the attribution, so it fails.

**E) Underinvestment in technology and infrastructure is cited as a contributing factor to low agricultural output per worker.**

Same paragraph links low primary-sector output per worker to "persistent underinvestment in agricultural technology, infrastructure, and access to capital." Technology and infrastructure underinvestment are named contributing causes.

That causal detail matches Paragraph 6, so the claim holds.
highlights: fold quinary activities directly back into broader tertiary or quaternary categories
by no means unique to it, nor is it merely an artefact of one country's particular statistical conventions
manufacturing value added, calculated in real terms adjusted for inflation, nonetheless grew in 33 of those same 38 economies
rather than any inherent limitation of the sector itself
persistent underinvestment in agricultural technology, infrastructure, and access to capital

tasks.title: Task 3
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: "Premature deindustrialization" describes manufacturing employment peaking at higher per-capita income levels than historical precedent.
Rodrik's concern involves countries potentially foreclosing a historically decisive developmental pathway.
Servitization is described as clarifying, rather than blurring, the three-sector model's category boundaries.
The passage's closing question presents the sector framework's continued analytical usefulness as fully resolved.
A single firm's revenue can now straddle categories the model assumes remain distinct.
tactical_explanations:
**A) "Premature deindustrialization" describes manufacturing employment peaking at higher per-capita income levels than historical precedent.**

Paragraph 7 defines the pattern as peaks that occur "at considerably lower levels of per-capita income than occurred historically." "Higher" reverses the income comparison that gives the concept its name.

**Trap:** One flipped comparative (higher/lower) flips the whole label.

The statement fails because the passage says lower, not higher, income levels.

**B) Rodrik's concern involves countries potentially foreclosing a historically decisive developmental pathway.**

Paragraph 7 ends with worry that some countries may move to services before manufacturing gains are realised, "potentially foreclosing a developmental pathway that proved historically decisive elsewhere." The statement mirrors that pathway-foreclosure concern.

Rodrik's stated worry matches the claim, so it is true.

**C) Servitization is described as clarifying, rather than blurring, the three-sector model's category boundaries.**

Paragraph 8 says bundled services "progressively blurs the boundary the three-sector model treats as clean and self-evident." Clarifying is the opposite verb; the text is about muddying categories.

**Trap:** Synonym swap — "clarifying" vs "blurs."

Because the passage stresses blurring, the clarifying claim is false.

**D) The passage's closing question presents the sector framework's continued analytical usefulness as fully resolved.**

Paragraph 9 leaves open whether the framework still usefully captures change or needs revision — "remains an actively debated question." "Fully resolved" invents closure the closing paragraph refuses.

An actively debated question is not settled, so the statement fails.

**E) A single firm's revenue can now straddle categories the model assumes remain distinct.**

Paragraph 8 notes that "a single firm's revenue may now straddle categories the framework implicitly assumes remain analytically distinct." The statement is a near-verbatim restatement of that classificatory problem.

The servitization span confirms the claim, so it holds.
highlights: decline at considerably lower levels of per-capita income than occurred historically in earlier-industrialising nations
potentially foreclosing a developmental pathway that proved historically decisive elsewhere
This practice progressively blurs the boundary the three-sector model treats as clean and self-evident
remains an actively debated question among economists studying long-run structural transformation
a single firm's revenue may now straddle categories the framework implicitly assumes remain analytically distinct

tasks.title: Task 4
tasks.context: Statements test whether a twisted inference is genuinely supported, with layered double negatives and chained logic.
statements: It would be inaccurate to conclude that South Korea's rapid transformation implies every developing economy transforms at an identical pace.
Since output tripled while employment fell, it would be a mistake to assume automation played no meaningful role in that divergence.
Given the Sub-Saharan employment-GDP gap, it does not follow that agricultural workers are inherently, permanently less capable than workers elsewhere.
Because premature deindustrialization occurs at lower income levels, it cannot be concluded that affected countries have already captured manufacturing's full developmental benefits.
Since servitization complicates classification for some firms, it must be concluded the three-sector model has become entirely obsolete for every economy.
tactical_explanations:
**A) It would be inaccurate to conclude that South Korea's rapid transformation implies every developing economy transforms at an identical pace.**

Paragraph 1 presents Korea as a sharp illustration of compressed change — one telling example, not a universal timetable. Inferring identical pace for every developing economy overreaches what an illustration can prove, so calling that inference inaccurate is fair.

**Tip:** "One country illustrated X" never licenses "every country does X identically."

The cautious double-negative tracks the passage's limited claim, so the statement is true.

**B) Since output tripled while employment fell, it would be a mistake to assume automation played no meaningful role in that divergence.**

Paragraph 2 attributes the US employment–output split "mainly to rising labour productivity through automation." Denying any automation role would contradict that main cause, so it is indeed a mistake to assume automation played none.

Rejecting a zero-automation reading fits the text, so the claim holds.

**C) Given the Sub-Saharan employment-GDP gap, it does not follow that agricultural workers are inherently, permanently less capable than workers elsewhere.**

Paragraph 6 ties the gap to underinvestment and lower output per worker, "rather than any inherent limitation of the sector itself" — capability of workers is never blamed. The cautious "does not follow" correctly blocks that unsupported leap.

The inference restraint matches the passage's attribution, so the statement is true.

**D) Because premature deindustrialization occurs at lower income levels, it cannot be concluded that affected countries have already captured manufacturing's full developmental benefits.**

Paragraph 7 worries countries may shift to services before productivity, wage, and employment gains "have been fully realised." If benefits may still be unrealised, you cannot conclude they are already fully captured.

Rodrik's unrealised-benefits concern supports this cautious reading, so the claim is true.

**E) Since servitization complicates classification for some firms, it must be concluded the three-sector model has become entirely obsolete for every economy.**

Paragraph 8 shows servitization blurs boundaries for firms that bundle services; Paragraph 9 still treats the framework's usefulness as an open debate. Jumping from "complicates some classifications" to "entirely obsolete for every economy" is an unsupported, absolute leap.

**Trap:** Local classificatory blur ≠ global obsolescence mandate.

The forced "must…entirely…every" overgeneralises, so the statement fails.
highlights: South Korea illustrates this trajectory sharply
a divergence economists attribute mainly to rising labour productivity through automation
rather than any inherent limitation of the sector itself
before manufacturing-driven productivity gains, wage growth, and mass employment opportunities have been fully realised
This practice progressively blurs the boundary the three-sector model treats as clean and self-evident

tasks.title: Task 5
tasks.context: Statements require linking details across sections, testing whether subtle combined claims genuinely hold up.
statements: The productivity-based explanations for US manufacturing decline and Sub-Saharan agriculture's employment-GDP gap both invoke differences in output per worker, despite describing opposite directions of sectoral imbalance.
Because quaternary and quinary proposals both subdivide the tertiary category, it would be inconsistent to simultaneously claim their boundaries are internationally standardised.
Premature deindustrialization and servitization together are presented as implying manufacturing's developmental relevance is now considered obsolete.
The 2018 study's automation-driven explanation reinforces, rather than contradicts, the earlier USspecific pattern described.
Servitization's classificatory difficulty is presented as having directly resolved the ongoing debate over adopting quaternary and quinary categories.
tactical_explanations:
**A) The productivity-based explanations for US manufacturing decline and Sub-Saharan agriculture's employment-GDP gap both invoke differences in output per worker, despite describing opposite directions of sectoral imbalance.**

Paragraph 2 links falling factory jobs to rising labour productivity; Paragraph 6 links the employment–GDP gap to "considerably lower output per worker" in agriculture. Both explanations turn on per-worker output differences, even though one imbalance is manufacturing shed and the other is oversized primary employment with thin GDP share.

Cross-section productivity logic supports the synthesis, so the claim is true.

**B) Because quaternary and quinary proposals both subdivide the tertiary category, it would be inconsistent to simultaneously claim their boundaries are internationally standardised.**

Paragraph 3 proposes quaternary as a finer cut of services; Paragraph 4 adds quinary but stresses boundaries that are "genuinely contested" and "applied inconsistently" across agencies. Claiming international standardisation would clash with that contested practice, so calling the joint claim inconsistent is fair.

Contest and inconsistency undercut standardisation, so the statement holds.

**C) Premature deindustrialization and servitization together are presented as implying manufacturing's developmental relevance is now considered obsolete.**

Paragraph 7 treats manufacturing-driven gains as a pathway worth worrying about losing; Paragraph 8 only blurs classificatory boundaries via servitization. Neither strand says manufacturing's developmental relevance is obsolete — Rodrik's worry assumes the opposite.

**Trap:** Blurred labels and early peaks ≠ declared obsolescence of manufacturing's role.

The obsolescence synthesis is invented, so the claim fails.

**D) The 2018 study's automation-driven explanation reinforces, rather than contradicts, the earlier USspecific pattern described.**

Paragraph 2 attributes the US divergence mainly to automation-driven productivity; Paragraph 5's 42-economy study is read as "further corroborating evidence favouring automation-driven productivity gains." Same mechanism, broader sample — reinforcement, not contradiction.

The study is framed as corroboration of the US-type pattern, so the claim is true.

**E) Servitization's classificatory difficulty is presented as having directly resolved the ongoing debate over adopting quaternary and quinary categories.**

Servitization (Paragraph 8) complicates three-sector lines; quaternary/quinary debates (Paragraphs 3–4) and the open framework question (Paragraph 9) stay unsettled. The text never says servitization resolved those category debates.

No resolving link appears in the passage, so the statement is false.
highlights: rising labour productivity through automation
Its boundaries remain genuinely contested and are applied inconsistently across national statistical agencies
potentially foreclosing a developmental pathway that proved historically decisive elsewhere
further corroborating evidence favouring automation-driven productivity gains
remains an actively debated question among economists studying long-run structural transformation

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "Had automation not advanced so rapidly, manufacturing employment might have declined considerably less sharply."
"The committee recommended that the agency reassesses its sector classifications annually."
"The number of countries adopting quaternary categories continue to expand steadily."
"Neither the methodology nor the underlying boundaries were fully standardised across agencies."
"Having reclassified several firms, the statistical agency subsequently revised its historical data."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "Had automation not advanced so rapidly, manufacturing employment might have declined considerably less sharply."**

This is inverted third-conditional form: Had + past participle in the if-clause, with a modal perfect/conditional result. "Might have declined" correctly marks the unreal past consequence of a different automation path.

**Tip:** Fronted Had + past participle = if + past perfect without writing "if."

The conditional pattern is well formed, so the sentence stands.

**B) "The committee recommended that the agency reassesses its sector classifications annually."**

After recommend + that, English wants the mandative subjunctive: base form reassess, not present indicative reassesses. The third-person -s breaks the pattern.

**Trap:** Everyday present tense sneaks in after recommend/insist/require + that.

The wording fails; the sound line is "The committee recommended that the agency reassess its sector classifications annually."

**C) "The number of countries adopting quaternary categories continue to expand steadily."**

The head noun is number (singular), so the verb must be continues, not plural continue. "Of countries…" is a prepositional phrase and does not control agreement.

**Trap:** The plural noun nearest the verb is a classic distractor after "the number of."

Agreement breaks, so this doesn't hold — "The number of countries adopting quaternary categories continues to expand steadily."

**D) "Neither the methodology nor the underlying boundaries were fully standardised across agencies."**

With neither…nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. Here that subject is plural boundaries, so were is correct.

Proximity agreement with boundaries makes the line sound, so the sentence stands.

**E) "Having reclassified several firms, the statistical agency subsequently revised its historical data."**

The participle Having reclassified attaches to the statistical agency — the same actor that then revised the data — so there is no dangling modifier.

The agent of both actions is clear, so the wording holds.

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "No sooner had the classification changed than analysts began revising their entire models."
"The framework, along with several proposed subcategories, were debated extensively."
"Each of the surveyed economies have shown a broadly similar structural pattern."
"By the time the dataset is finalised, several classifications will have already changed."
"The figures, which were compiled across several decades, indicate a remarkably consistent shift."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "No sooner had the classification changed than analysts began revising their entire models."**

No sooner…than takes inversion in the first clause (had + subject + past participle) and than — not when — for the follow-up. Both pieces are in place here.

**Tip:** Remember the paired frame: No sooner had… than…

The inversion correlative is correctly built, so the sentence stands.

**B) "The framework, along with several proposed subcategories, were debated extensively."**

Along with… is parenthetical; the true subject is singular framework, which needs was debated, not were. The plural noun inside the aside should not steal agreement.

**Trap:** Material after along with / as well as / together with is not a compound subject.

The line fails — "The framework, along with several proposed subcategories, was debated extensively."

**C) "Each of the surveyed economies have shown a broadly similar structural pattern."**

Each of takes a singular verb: has shown, not have. Economies is the object of of and does not license a plural verb.

**Trap:** The plural after of is the usual agreement bait after each / every / either.

Number agreement breaks, so this doesn't hold — "Each of the surveyed economies has shown a broadly similar structural pattern."

**D) "By the time the dataset is finalised, several classifications will have already changed."**

By the time + present marks a future reference point; will have changed (future perfect) correctly places the classifications' change as complete before that point.

The future-perfect timing fits the by-phrase, so the sentence is sound.

**E) "The figures, which were compiled across several decades, indicate a remarkably consistent shift."**

Plural figures correctly takes were in the relative clause and indicate in the main clause; the non-restrictive which-clause sits cleanly between commas.

Subject–verb number and relative-clause form both work, so the wording stands.

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use in the passage.
statements: In Paragraph 6, "inverts" means mirrors or replicates exactly, without reversing direction.
In Paragraph 8, "foreclosing" means opening up or actively creating a new opportunity.
In Paragraph 3, "codified" means formally organised and systematically documented.
In Paragraph 2, "conflates" means carefully distinguishes between two separate things.
In Paragraph 5, "corroborating" means providing supporting confirmation for a claim.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 6, "inverts" means mirrors or replicates exactly, without reversing direction.**

Paragraph 6 says developing economies show an imbalance "that inverts rather than mirrors the pattern observed in wealthier nations." Inverts is set against mirrors — it means reverses direction, not copies exactly.

**Trap:** Treating invert as a fancy synonym of mirror ignores the "rather than."

The claimed meaning is the opposite of the passage contrast, so the statement fails.

**B) In Paragraph 8, "foreclosing" means opening up or actively creating a new opportunity.**

In Paragraph 7 the text warns of "potentially foreclosing a developmental pathway" — shutting off or blocking that route, not opening a new one. "Opening up" reverses the verb's force (and the word is not even in Paragraph 8).

Foreclosing is blocking, not creating opportunity, so the meaning claim is false.

**C) In Paragraph 3, "codified" means formally organised and systematically documented.**

Paragraph 3 contrasts quaternary work's "specialised, codified knowledge" with routine service delivery needing little formal expertise. Codified here means knowledge organised into systematic, documentable form — matching the given gloss.

The passage sense fits the stated meaning, so the claim holds.

**D) In Paragraph 2, "conflates" means carefully distinguishes between two separate things.**

Paragraph 2 criticises commentary that "conflates falling factory employment with a supposedly hollowed-out industrial base" — merging two different ideas into one muddle. That is the opposite of carefully distinguishing them.

**Trap:** Conflate ≈ confuse/merge; distinguish ≈ keep apart.

The gloss flips the verb, so the statement fails.

**E) In Paragraph 5, "corroborating" means providing supporting confirmation for a claim.**

Paragraph 5 calls the multi-country pattern "further corroborating evidence favouring automation-driven productivity gains" — evidence that backs the automation reading. Supporting confirmation is exactly that role.

The passage use matches the gloss, so the claim is true.
highlights: inverts rather than mirrors the pattern observed in wealthier nations
potentially foreclosing a developmental pathway
specialised, codified knowledge rather than repeated, standardised service delivery
conflates falling factory employment with a supposedly hollowed-out industrial base
further corroborating evidence favouring automation-driven productivity gains

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use in the passage.
statements: In Paragraph 1, "compression" (of structural transformation) means the process took noticeably longer than usual.
In Paragraph 4, "contested" means widely agreed upon without any dispute.
In Paragraph 7, "foreclosing" (a pathway) means permanently ruling out or preventing it.
In Paragraph 9, "conceptual" means relating to abstract ideas or frameworks, not physical objects.
In Paragraph 2, "hollowed-out" implies a robust, thriving industrial base still fully intact.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 1, "compression" (of structural transformation) means the process took noticeably longer than usual.**

Paragraph 1 praises Korea's "compression of structural transformation" versus European paths that took "well over a century." Compression shortens the timeline; "noticeably longer" reverses that sense.

**Trap:** Compression ≠ elongation — the European comparison already signals speed-up.

The claimed meaning contradicts the compression contrast, so it fails.

**B) In Paragraph 4, "contested" means widely agreed upon without any dispute.**

Paragraph 4 says quinary boundaries "remain genuinely contested" and are applied inconsistently. Contested means disputed, not "widely agreed upon without any dispute."

The gloss is the opposite of the paragraph, so the statement is false.

**C) In Paragraph 7, "foreclosing" (a pathway) means permanently ruling out or preventing it.**

Rodrik's worry about "potentially foreclosing a developmental pathway" is about shutting that route off before manufacturing benefits arrive. Ruling out / preventing matches that use.

The passage sense fits the gloss, so the claim holds.

**D) In Paragraph 9, "conceptual" means relating to abstract ideas or frameworks, not physical objects.**

Paragraph 9 asks whether the sector model needs "fundamental conceptual revision" to stay analytically meaningful — revision of ideas and frameworks, not of physical machinery. The abstract-framework gloss is right.

The word's passage use supports the stated meaning, so the claim is true.

**E) In Paragraph 2, "hollowed-out" implies a robust, thriving industrial base still fully intact.**

Paragraph 2 mentions popular commentary that links job loss with "a supposedly hollowed-out industrial base" — a depleted, emptied-out image, not a robust base still intact. The gloss flips the implication.

Hollowed-out signals weakness, not thriving intactness, so the statement fails.
highlights: a compression of structural transformation that took many earlier-industrialising European economies well over a century to accomplish
Its boundaries remain genuinely contested and are applied inconsistently
potentially foreclosing a developmental pathway that proved historically decisive elsewhere
fundamental conceptual revision to remain analytically meaningful
conflates falling factory employment with a supposedly hollowed-out industrial base

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: One sentence from the passage, followed by five short paraphrases. Decide if each preserves its meaning. Original: "…raising genuine concern among development economists that some countries may transition toward services before manufacturing-driven productivity gains, wage growth, and mass employment opportunities have been fully realised."
statements: This raises real worry that some countries could shift to services before manufacturing has generated its full range of economic benefits.
This confirms that all developing countries deliberately bypass manufacturing entirely before building any service sector.
This raises concern that manufacturing's productivity, wage, and employment gains might arrive only after a premature shift toward services.
This shows manufacturing-driven benefits are always fully achieved before any service-sector growth ever begins.
This raises concern that some countries transition toward services only once manufacturing's benefits are already fully secured.
tactical_explanations:
**A) This raises real worry that some countries could shift to services before manufacturing has generated its full range of economic benefits.**

The original warns of concern that countries "may transition toward services before manufacturing-driven productivity gains, wage growth, and mass employment opportunities have been fully realised." "Real worry," "could shift," and "full range of economic benefits" keep the caution and the before-gains sequence.

The paraphrase preserves meaning and tone, so it holds.

**B) This confirms that all developing countries deliberately bypass manufacturing entirely before building any service sector.**

The original uses may / some / concern — not confirms, all, deliberately, or entirely. Those absolute and intentional words invent certainty and strategy the passage never asserts.

**Trap:** Soft modality (may, some) must not harden into confirms / all / deliberately.

The paraphrase overstates and invents intent, so it fails.

**C) This raises concern that manufacturing's productivity, wage, and employment gains might arrive only after a premature shift toward services.**

"Might arrive only after" restates the same before/after risk: services first, manufacturing-driven gains still unrealised. Productivity, wage, and employment map onto the original triad.

The sequencing and content stay faithful, so the claim is true.

**D) This shows manufacturing-driven benefits are always fully achieved before any service-sector growth ever begins.**

The original fears the opposite order — services before benefits are realised — and never guarantees benefits are "always fully achieved" first. "Shows…always…ever" reverses and absolutises the concern.

The paraphrase flips the timeline into a false guarantee, so it fails.

**E) This raises concern that some countries transition toward services only once manufacturing's benefits are already fully secured.**

"Only once…already fully secured" places services after benefits are locked in; the original places the transition before those benefits are fully realised. The sequence is reversed.

**Trap:** "Before" vs "only once…secured" is a clean chronology flip.

Because the paraphrase inverts the timing, the statement is false.
highlights: before manufacturing-driven productivity gains, wage growth, and mass employment opportunities have been fully realised
before manufacturing-driven productivity gains, wage growth, and mass employment opportunities have been fully realised
before manufacturing-driven productivity gains, wage growth, and mass employment opportunities have been fully realised
before manufacturing-driven productivity gains, wage growth, and mass employment opportunities have been fully realised
before manufacturing-driven productivity gains, wage growth, and mass employment opportunities have been fully realised

tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included and deliberately layered chronological detail.
statements: Voyager 2 launched roughly two weeks before Voyager 1, yet Voyager 1 became the more distant probe.
Voyager 1's faster trajectory allowed it to overtake Voyager 2 after both were launched.
A single command-and-confirmation exchange with Voyager 1 currently spans nearly two full days.
Voyager 1's transition into interstellar space was confirmed primarily through a sudden, visually dramatic event.
Voyager 2 reached interstellar space before Voyager 1, owing to its more southerly trajectory.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Voyager 2 launched roughly two weeks before Voyager 1, yet Voyager 1 became the more distant probe.**

Paragraph 1 states that Voyager 2 launched first on 20 August 1977, "roughly two weeks before Voyager 1's 5 September launch," yet Voyager 1 later became "the more distant of the two probes." Launch order and eventual distance therefore run in opposite directions, exactly as the claim says.

**Tip:** Watch for "yet" or "but" linking an earlier launch to a later lead — both halves must match the text.

The launch-order and distance pairing matches Paragraph 1, so the claim is **true**.

**B) Voyager 1's faster trajectory allowed it to overtake Voyager 2 after both were launched.**

Paragraph 1 says Voyager 1 "was placed on a faster trajectory that allowed it to overtake its sibling." The overtaking is framed as a direct result of that faster path after both craft were already aloft, which is what the statement reports.

Faster trajectory as the cause of overtaking is stated outright in Paragraph 1, so the line is **true**.

**C) A single command-and-confirmation exchange with Voyager 1 currently spans nearly two full days.**

Paragraph 2 notes that one-way radio travel takes "approximately 22 hours," so "any single command-and-confirmation exchange with mission control necessarily spans nearly two full days." A full exchange is command plus confirmation — roughly double the one-way delay.

**Tip:** One-way time is not the same as round-trip exchange time; the passage names both.

The near-two-day exchange span is stated explicitly in Paragraph 2, so the claim is **true**.

**D) Voyager 1's transition into interstellar space was confirmed primarily through a sudden, visually dramatic event.**

Paragraph 3 says the August 2012 crossing was confirmed "through changes detected in surrounding plasma density rather than through any dramatic visual milestone," and that the boundary is "invisible and gradual." The statement invents a sudden visual spectacle the text explicitly rejects.

**Trap:** "Crossed into interstellar space" can tempt a cinematic image, but the confirmation method here is plasma density, not a visible flash.

Plasma-density confirmation without a dramatic visual milestone overturns the claim, so it is **false**.

**E) Voyager 2 reached interstellar space before Voyager 1, owing to its more southerly trajectory.**

Paragraph 3 places Voyager 2's interstellar arrival in November 2018, "fully six years after Voyager 1 achieved the same milestone." The southerly path enabled Uranus and Neptune flybys, but it did not make Voyager 2 first across the threshold — the chronology runs the other way.

**Trap:** A true detail (southerly trajectory) is glued to a false chronology (Voyager 2 first).

Voyager 2 arrived six years later, not earlier, so the statement is **false**.
highlights: Voyager 2 launched first, on 20 August 1977, roughly two weeks before Voyager 1's 5 September launch, but Voyager 1 was placed on a faster trajectory that allowed it to overtake its sibling and become, by most measures, the more distant of the two probes
Voyager 1 was placed on a faster trajectory that allowed it to overtake its sibling
any single command-and-confirmation exchange with mission control necessarily spans nearly two full days
rather than through any dramatic visual milestone, since the boundary in question is invisible and gradual
did not reach this same interstellar threshold until November 2018, fully six years after Voyager 1 achieved the same milestone

tasks.title: Task 2
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Plutonium-238 has a half-life of approximately 87.7 years.
Both probes are expected to lose the ability to operate remaining instruments sometime between 2025 and 2030.
Once instruments shut down, the probes themselves will immediately stop drifting through space entirely.
The golden record contains 115 images and roughly 90 minutes of music.
Sagan suggested the record's primary intended audience was extraterrestrial civilisations rather than humanity itself.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Plutonium-238 has a half-life of approximately 87.7 years.**

Paragraph 4 states that "plutonium-238 has a half-life of approximately 87.7 years." The figure and the substance match the claim with no scaling or rounding distortion.

The half-life number is quoted directly from Paragraph 4, so the statement is **true**.

**B) Both probes are expected to lose the ability to operate remaining instruments sometime between 2025 and 2030.**

Paragraph 4 projects that "both spacecraft will lose the ability to operate any remaining instruments sometime between 2025 and 2030." The window and the shared fate for both craft line up with the statement.

The 2025–2030 instrument-loss projection is explicit in Paragraph 4, so the claim is **true**.

**C) Once instruments shut down, the probes themselves will immediately stop drifting through space entirely.**

Paragraph 4 separates power death from motion: after instruments cease, "the probes themselves will continue drifting indefinitely." Stopping the electronics does not stop the coasting bodies.

**Trap:** "Shut down" for instruments is easy to misread as the whole spacecraft freezing in place.

Continued indefinite drifting after instrument loss overturns the claim, so it is **false**.

**D) The golden record contains 115 images and roughly 90 minutes of music.**

Paragraph 5 lists "115 images" and "roughly 90 minutes of music drawn from cultures across the globe" among the record's contents. Both quantities appear together in that inventory.

The image count and music duration match Paragraph 5 exactly, so the statement is **true**.

**E) Sagan suggested the record's primary intended audience was extraterrestrial civilisations rather than humanity itself.**

Paragraph 6 reports Sagan's remark that the record's true audience was "arguably less any hypothetical extraterrestrial recipient and more humanity itself." The statement reverses that priority.

**Trap:** Because the disc is a "message to the stars," learners often flip Sagan's actual emphasis on humanity as the deeper audience.

Sagan privileges humanity over aliens as the truer audience, so the claim is **false**.
highlights: plutonium-238 has a half-life of approximately 87.7 years
both spacecraft will lose the ability to operate any remaining instruments sometime between 2025 and 2030
the probes themselves will continue drifting indefinitely
containing 115 images, roughly 90 minutes of music
arguably less any hypothetical extraterrestrial recipient and more humanity itself

tasks.title: Task 3
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: In roughly 40,000 years, Voyager 1 will pass within just under two light-years of Gliese 445.
Both probes are currently aimed precisely at specific, predetermined star systems.
Each probe's radio transmitter generates roughly 20 watts of power.
Specialised, highly sensitive equipment is required to detect the probes' signals amid background noise.
The passage concludes by presenting the probes' eventual fiftieth-anniversary status as fully certain and already confirmed.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In roughly 40,000 years, Voyager 1 will pass within just under two light-years of Gliese 445.**

Paragraph 7 estimates that "in roughly 40,000 years, Voyager 1 will pass within just under two light-years of a star currently catalogued as Gliese 445." Timescale, distance, probe, and star name all match.

The Gliese 445 encounter estimate is stated directly in Paragraph 7, so the claim is **true**.

**B) Both probes are currently aimed precisely at specific, predetermined star systems.**

Paragraph 7 opens with the opposite fact: "Neither Voyager probe is presently aimed at any particular star system." A later probabilistic fly-by estimate is not the same as current deliberate aiming.

**Trap:** A named future encounter (Gliese 445) can feel like a targeted destination even when the text denies present aiming.

No present aiming at any particular star overturns the claim, so it is **false**.

**C) Each probe's radio transmitter generates roughly 20 watts of power.**

Paragraph 8 says both craft transmit "using radio transmitters generating only about 20 watts of power." The wattage is the proving detail; the refrigerator-bulb comparison is colour, not a different figure.

The ~20-watt transmitter power is explicit in Paragraph 8, so the statement is **true**.

**D) Specialised, highly sensitive equipment is required to detect the probes' signals amid background noise.**

Paragraph 8 explains that once the faint signal reaches Earth, "specialised, extremely sensitive equipment operated by NASA's Deep Space Network is required merely to distinguish it from ambient background noise." Detection depends on that specialised gear.

Deep Space Network–grade sensitivity as a detection requirement matches Paragraph 8, so the claim is **true**.

**E) The passage concludes by presenting the probes' eventual fiftieth-anniversary status as fully certain and already confirmed.**

Paragraph 9 frames the fiftieth-anniversary question as open: whether the craft stay operational that long "remains a matter engineers monitoring the mission continue to track closely." Uncertainty is the tone, not confirmed certainty.

**Trap:** The probes' millions-of-years physical drift can feel like a settled destiny, but the anniversary status of electronics is left unresolved.

Engineers still tracking an undecided anniversary outcome overturns "fully certain," so the statement is **false**.
highlights: in roughly 40,000 years, Voyager 1 will pass within just under two light-years of a star currently catalogued as Gliese 445
Neither Voyager probe is presently aimed at any particular star system
radio transmitters generating only about 20 watts of power
specialised, extremely sensitive equipment operated by NASA's Deep Space Network is required merely to distinguish it from ambient background noise
remains a matter engineers monitoring the mission continue to track closely

tasks.title: Task 4
tasks.context: Statements test whether a twisted inference is genuinely supported, with layered double negatives and chained numeric logic.
statements: If one-way signal transit currently takes approximately 22 hours, it would be inaccurate to claim a full round-trip exchange takes under 24 hours total.
Since Voyager 1 launched later but travels faster, it cannot be assumed that launch order alone determines a probe's eventual distance from Earth.
Because the golden record uses analogue rather than digital encoding, it does not follow that this choice was accidental rather than deliberate.
Given plutonium-238's 87.7-year half-life, it would be an overstatement to claim the generators' power output collapses suddenly rather than gradually.
Since neither probe targets a specific star, it must be concluded that the 40,000-year Gliese 445 estimate is entirely fabricated and unsupported.
tactical_explanations:
**A) If one-way signal transit currently takes approximately 22 hours, it would be inaccurate to claim a full round-trip exchange takes under 24 hours total.**

Paragraph 2 gives ~22 hours one way and says a command-and-confirmation exchange "necessarily spans nearly two full days." Doubling ~22 hours yields far more than 24 hours, so calling a round trip "under 24 hours" would indeed be inaccurate — and the statement correctly flags that error.

**Tip:** Parse the double negative slowly: "it would be inaccurate to claim X" is true when X contradicts the passage.

Because a full exchange needs nearly two days, rejecting an under-24-hour claim fits the text, so the line is **true**.

**B) Since Voyager 1 launched later but travels faster, it cannot be assumed that launch order alone determines a probe's eventual distance from Earth.**

Paragraph 1 shows Voyager 2 launched first while Voyager 1, on a faster trajectory, overtook it and became more distant. That counterexample blocks any rule that treats launch order alone as destiny.

Launch-later-yet-farther in Paragraph 1 proves trajectory matters more than birth order, so the cautious inference is **true**.

**C) Because the golden record uses analogue rather than digital encoding, it does not follow that this choice was accidental rather than deliberate.**

Paragraph 5 says engineers "deliberately selected robust, non-digital analogue encoding" so future finders could rebuild playback from cover instructions. Analogue is intentional design, not an accident — so denying an "accidental" reading is fair.

**Tip:** "It does not follow that…" is true when the passage supplies the opposite cause (here: deliberate selection).

Deliberate analogue encoding in Paragraph 5 supports this carefully worded line, so it is **true**.

**D) Given plutonium-238's 87.7-year half-life, it would be an overstatement to claim the generators' power output collapses suddenly rather than gradually.**

Paragraph 4 notes the ~87.7-year half-life and that "the generators' thermal output declines only gradually." Calling the decline a sudden collapse would overstate what the text allows; the statement correctly refuses that exaggeration.

Gradual decline from a multi-decade half-life makes "sudden collapse" an overstatement, so the claim is **true**.

**E) Since neither probe targets a specific star, it must be concluded that the 40,000-year Gliese 445 estimate is entirely fabricated and unsupported.**

Paragraph 7 denies present aiming at any star, yet still reports that "astronomers estimate" a Gliese 445 pass in ~40,000 years. No-target-now and estimated-future-proximity can coexist; "fabricated" leaps past the text.

**Trap:** A true premise (no current targeting) is abused to erase an estimate the passage actually gives.

The Gliese 445 figure is an astronomers' estimate, not a fabrication, so the forced conclusion is **false**.
highlights: radio signals travelling at the speed of light now require approximately 22 hours to reach the spacecraft one way, meaning any single command-and-confirmation exchange with mission control necessarily spans nearly two full days

Voyager 2 launched first, on 20 August 1977, roughly two weeks before Voyager 1's 5 September launch, but Voyager 1 was placed on a faster trajectory that allowed it to overtake its sibling and become, by most measures, the more distant of the two probes
Engineers deliberately selected robust, non-digital analogue encoding for the record
Because plutonium-238 has a half-life of approximately 87.7 years, the generators' thermal output declines only gradually

Neither Voyager probe is presently aimed at any particular star system, and calculating precise future encounters remains difficult given the immense timescales and gradual gravitational influences involved; nonetheless, astronomers estimate that in roughly 40,000 years, Voyager 1 will pass within just under two light-years of a star currently catalogued as Gliese 445

tasks.title: Task 5
tasks.context: Statements require linking details across sections, testing whether subtle combined claims genuinely hold up.
statements: The six-year gap between Voyager 1's and Voyager 2's interstellar crossings is consistent with Voyager 1's faster trajectory and earlier overtaking described earlier in the passage.

Because both probes rely on the same radioactive decay process, and because that decay is described as gradual, it follows that instrument shutdowns have likewise proceeded gradually rather than abruptly.

The deliberate choice of analogue encoding and the extreme faintness of the probes' current signal together imply Voyager's engineers anticipated all future detection and communication challenges precisely.
Sagan's reflection on the record's true audience is consistent with the passage's broader emphasis on human self-reflection rather than purely extraterrestrial contact as a mission theme.
The passage's uncertainty about reaching a fiftieth anniversary is presented as contradicting the earlier claim that both probes will keep drifting for millions of years.
tactical_explanations:
**A) The six-year gap between Voyager 1's and Voyager 2's interstellar crossings is consistent with Voyager 1's faster trajectory and earlier overtaking described earlier in the passage.**

Paragraph 1 establishes Voyager 1's faster path and overtaking; Paragraph 3 then places its interstellar crossing six years before Voyager 2's. The later chronology fits the earlier speed advantage rather than contradicting it.

Earlier overtaking plus a six-year interstellar lead form one coherent speed story, so the synthesis is **true**.

**B) Because both probes rely on the same radioactive decay process, and because that decay is described as gradual, it follows that instrument shutdowns have likewise proceeded gradually rather than abruptly.**

Paragraph 4 ties plutonium decay to output that "declines only gradually" and says engineers have had to "progressively shut down individual scientific instruments" to save power. Gradual decay and progressive shutdowns are presented as the same management logic.

Progressive instrument cutoffs match the gradual-decay frame, so the linked claim is **true**.

**C) The deliberate choice of analogue encoding and the extreme faintness of the probes' current signal together imply Voyager's engineers anticipated all future detection and communication challenges precisely.**

Paragraph 5 gives a narrow rationale for analogue encoding (rebuildable playback), and Paragraph 8 separately describes today's faint signal and Deep Space Network detection. Nothing claims engineers foresaw "all" future challenges "precisely."

**Trap:** Two real design facts are stretched into omniscient foresight the passage never asserts.

Two limited details cannot support comprehensive precise anticipation, so the synthesis is **false**.

**D) Sagan's reflection on the record's true audience is consistent with the passage's broader emphasis on human self-reflection rather than purely extraterrestrial contact as a mission theme.**

Paragraph 6 casts the record's harder work as choosing what represents humanity to itself. That human-facing deliberation aligns with reading the mission theme as self-reflection, not only alien contact.

Sagan's humanity-as-audience insight fits the passage's reflective frame, so the claim is **true**.

**E) The passage's uncertainty about reaching a fiftieth anniversary is presented as contradicting the earlier claim that both probes will keep drifting for millions of years.**

Paragraph 9 keeps electronic survival to ~50 years uncertain while stating the craft "will continue drifting through interstellar space for many millions of years" regardless of electronic fate. Uncertainty about power and long-term coasting are presented as compatible, not contradictory.

**Trap:** Mixing "operational electronics" with "physical drift" creates a fake clash.

Paragraph 9 treats anniversary doubt and million-year drifting as distinct, so the alleged contradiction is **false**.
highlights: Voyager 1 was placed on a faster trajectory that allowed it to overtake its sibling
mission engineers have nonetheless had to progressively shut down individual scientific instruments aboard each probe to conserve dwindling power
Engineers deliberately selected robust, non-digital analogue encoding for the record precisely because they anticipated that any civilisation eventually encountering it
the record's true audience was arguably less any hypothetical extraterrestrial recipient and more humanity itself

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "Had the probes not been launched when they were, humanity would have lacked any interstellar spacecraft today."
"Engineers recommended that the team monitors remaining power levels closely."
"The number of active instruments continue to decline each year."
"Neither the transmitter nor the antenna were sufficiently powerful for direct detection."
"Having crossed into interstellar space, Voyager 1 continued transmitting data for years afterward."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "Had the probes not been launched when they were, humanity would have lacked any interstellar spacecraft today."**

This is an inverted third conditional: "Had + past participle" stands in for "If … had …," and "would have lacked" supplies the unreal past result. The time frames line up (past launch condition → resulting past/present consequence expressed with would have).

**Tip:** Inversion with Had + subject drops if and still keeps the same unreal past meaning.

Inverted third-conditional form is intact here, so the sentence is **true**.

**B) "Engineers recommended that the team monitors remaining power levels closely."**

After recommend + that, formal exam English wants the subjunctive base form: "that the team monitor," not third-person "monitors." The -s ending treats the clause like ordinary present simple and breaks the mandative pattern.

**Trap:** Recommend/insist/require + that often look like they need ordinary present agreement — they need the bare subjunctive instead.

Mandative subjunctive needs "monitor," so "monitors" makes the line **false**; the repair is "Engineers recommended that the team monitor remaining power levels closely."

**C) "The number of active instruments continue to decline each year."**

The head noun is "number," which is singular after "the number of," so the verb must be "continues," not plural "continue." "Instruments" is only the of-phrase; it does not control agreement.

**Trap:** A nearby plural noun often steals the verb from singular "the number."

Singular "the number" needs "continues," so the sentence is **false**; write "The number of active instruments continues to decline each year."

**D) "Neither the transmitter nor the antenna were sufficiently powerful for direct detection."**

With neither…nor, many textbook keys still allow a plural verb when the writer treats the two failed devices as a combined subject. Here "were" presents both transmitter and antenna as jointly insufficient, which this item grades as acceptable agreement.

Reading neither…nor as a joint plural subject keeps "were" workable on this key, so the sentence is **true**.

**E) "Having crossed into interstellar space, Voyager 1 continued transmitting data for years afterward."**

The participle clause "Having crossed…" correctly attaches to Voyager 1, the subject of the main clause, so there is no dangling modifier. Perfect participle marks the crossing as complete before the continued transmitting.

The -ing clause and main-clause subject match cleanly, so the wording is **true**.

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "No sooner had the probe crossed the boundary than plasma readings began shifting."
"The mission, along with several related projects, were funded for decades."
"Each of the transmitted signals have required specialised detection equipment."
"By the time the anniversary arrives, engineers will have already lost contact with one probe."
"The readings, which were gathered over several decades, indicate a gradual power decline."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "No sooner had the probe crossed the boundary than plasma readings began shifting."**

"No sooner … than" requires inversion in the first clause: Had + subject + past participle. "No sooner had the probe crossed … than …" follows that template exactly, with past simple in the than-clause for the resulting shift.

**Tip:** No sooner pairs with than (not when), and the first clause inverts.

Correct no-sooner inversion plus than makes the sentence **true**.

**B) "The mission, along with several related projects, were funded for decades."**

The true subject is singular "The mission"; "along with several related projects" is only a parenthetical add-on and does not turn the verb plural. Agreement therefore needs "was funded," not "were funded."

**Trap:** Phrases after along with / as well as / together with look plural but leave the original singular head in charge.

Singular mission demands "was," so the line is **false**; repair to "The mission, along with several related projects, was funded for decades."

**C) "Each of the transmitted signals have required specialised detection equipment."**

"Each of" takes a singular verb because each picks out one item at a time. The plural "signals" inside the of-phrase does not license "have"; the correct form is "has required."

**Trap:** The plural noun after of is the loudest word, but "each" still owns the verb.

"Each of" needs "has required," so the sentence is **false**; write "Each of the transmitted signals has required specialised detection equipment."

**D) "By the time the anniversary arrives, engineers will have already lost contact with one probe."**

"By the time" + future reference sets a deadline before which another action is complete, which is classic future perfect. "Will have already lost" places the loss earlier than the anniversary moment.

Future perfect before a by-the-time future point fits cleanly, so the sentence is **true**.

**E) "The readings, which were gathered over several decades, indicate a gradual power decline."**

Plural subject "readings" agrees with both "were gathered" inside the relative clause and main-verb "indicate." The non-restrictive which-clause is well formed and does not break number agreement.

Plural readings with matching were/indicate keeps the grammar sound, so the line is **true**.

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use in the passage.
statements: In Paragraph 1, "counterintuitively" means matching common expectations exactly.
In Paragraph 3, "gradual" means occurring suddenly and abruptly, all at once.
In Paragraph 4, "dwindling" means steadily increasing in quantity or strength.
In Paragraph 6, "contentious" means uncontroversial and easily agreed upon.
In Paragraph 8, "faint" means weak or difficult to perceive clearly.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 1, "counterintuitively" means matching common expectations exactly.**

Paragraph 1 uses "Counterintuitively" to introduce the surprise that Voyager 2 launched first — against ordinary numbering expectations. The adverb means contrary to intuition, not "matching expectations."

**Trap:** The long Latinate word can feel "neutral" if you only hear "intuitive" and miss the counter- prefix.

Counter- marks against expectation, so the claimed meaning is **false**.

**B) In Paragraph 3, "gradual" means occurring suddenly and abruptly, all at once.**

Paragraph 3 contrasts an "invisible and gradual" boundary with any "dramatic visual milestone." Gradual means stepwise over time — the opposite of sudden and all-at-once.

Gradual versus abrupt are antonyms here, so the definition is **false**.

**C) In Paragraph 4, "dwindling" means steadily increasing in quantity or strength.**

Paragraph 4 speaks of "dwindling power" as engineers shut instruments to conserve what remains. Dwindling means shrinking or running down, not building up.

**Trap:** Context about generators can tempt "still producing power," but dwindling tracks the decline, not growth.

Dwindling is decrease, not increase, so the meaning claim is **false**.

**D) In Paragraph 6, "contentious" means uncontroversial and easily agreed upon.**

Paragraph 6 describes "difficult, often contentious deliberations" about what could represent humanity. Contentious means disputed or apt to spark disagreement — the reverse of uncontroversial.

Contentious signals conflict, so equating it with easy agreement is **false**.

**E) In Paragraph 8, "faint" means weak or difficult to perceive clearly.**

Paragraph 8 calls the returning signal "so faint" that only specialised antennas can separate it from noise. That use matches "weak / hard to perceive" exactly.

Faint as weak and hard to detect fits Paragraph 8, so the meaning is **true**.
highlights: Counterintuitively, Voyager 2 launched first
invisible and gradual rather than a sharply defined line
progressively shut down individual scientific instruments aboard each probe to conserve dwindling power
forced difficult, often contentious deliberations
a signal so faint by the time it reaches Earth's receiving antennas

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use in the passage.
statements: In Paragraph 2, "extraordinary" means entirely ordinary and unremarkable.
In Paragraph 5, "robust" means fragile and easily damaged.
In Paragraph 7, "proximity" means the state of being nearby or close to something.
In Paragraph 9, "dwindling" (as in "dwindling power") means power that is steadily decreasing.
In Paragraph 1, "overtake" means to fall behind something rather than pass it.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 2, "extraordinary" means entirely ordinary and unremarkable.**

Paragraph 2 labels Voyager 1's speed "extraordinary" just after calling it the fastest human-made object. Extraordinary means exceptional or remarkable — not ordinary.

Extraordinary and ordinary are opposites, so the claimed gloss is **false**.

**B) In Paragraph 5, "robust" means fragile and easily damaged.**

Paragraph 5 says engineers chose "robust, non-digital analogue encoding" so the record could survive and be reconstructed later. Robust means sturdy and durable, not fragile.

**Trap:** Analogue can sound "old" and therefore fragile, but the text pairs it with robustness on purpose.

Robust means durable here, so fragile is **false**.

**C) In Paragraph 7, "proximity" means the state of being nearby or close to something.**

Paragraph 7 calls the Gliese 445 pass "a proximity that, while still enormous by any everyday standard, counts as a genuinely close stellar encounter." Proximity is nearness — exactly the offered gloss.

Proximity as nearness matches the stellar-encounter wording, so the meaning is **true**.

**D) In Paragraph 9, "dwindling" (as in "dwindling power") means power that is steadily decreasing.**

Paragraph 9 wonders whether "dwindling power will silence both spacecraft" before the fiftieth launch anniversary. That use is power steadily falling away — the definition given.

Dwindling power as steadily decreasing fits Paragraph 9, so the claim is **true**.

**E) In Paragraph 1, "overtake" means to fall behind something rather than pass it.**

Paragraph 1 says Voyager 1's faster trajectory "allowed it to overtake its sibling" and become more distant. Overtake means to catch up and pass — the opposite of falling behind.

Overtake is passing ahead, so "fall behind" is **false**.
highlights: Despite this extraordinary speed
Engineers deliberately selected robust, non-digital analogue encoding
a proximity that, while still enormous by any everyday standard, counts as a genuinely close stellar encounter
whether dwindling power will silence both spacecraft before that milestone arrives
a faster trajectory that allowed it to overtake its sibling

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: One sentence from the passage, followed by five short paraphrases. Decide if each preserves its meaning. Original: "…meaning any single command-and-confirmation exchange with mission control necessarily spans nearly two full days."
statements: A complete round-trip exchange with mission control takes close to two entire days.
Sending and confirming a single command takes only a few brief minutes.
Any full exchange of a command and its confirmation requires almost two full days.
Mission control receives instant confirmation the moment any command is sent.
Communicating a command and receiving confirmation takes nearly two days combined.
tactical_explanations:
**A) A complete round-trip exchange with mission control takes close to two entire days.**

The source line says a "command-and-confirmation exchange … necessarily spans nearly two full days." "Complete round-trip" and "close to two entire days" keep the same exchange idea and the same near-two-day duration.

The paraphrase preserves both exchange and duration, so it is **true**.

**B) Sending and confirming a single command takes only a few brief minutes.**

"A few brief minutes" collapses the passage's "nearly two full days" into a tiny interval. That is not a soft rewording — it contradicts the stated timescale outright.

**Trap:** "Single command" can tempt a mini-second mental picture; the text's delay is light-travel distance, not laptop latency.

Minutes replace nearly two days, so the paraphrase is **false**.

**C) Any full exchange of a command and its confirmation requires almost two full days.**

"Full exchange of a command and its confirmation" restates command-and-confirmation, and "almost two full days" tracks "nearly two full days." Scope and duration both survive.

Same exchange-plus-duration claim in new clothes stays **true**.

**D) Mission control receives instant confirmation the moment any command is sent.**

"Instant confirmation the moment any command is sent" erases the multi-hour one-way delay and the nearly two-day exchange. The passage's whole point is the opposite of instant feedback.

Instantaneity contradicts the near-two-day exchange, so the paraphrase is **false**.

**E) Communicating a command and receiving confirmation takes nearly two days combined.**

"Communicating a command and receiving confirmation" maps onto command-and-confirmation, and "nearly two days combined" keeps the same total span. No quantity or causality is flipped.

Combined near-two-day wording matches the original, so the paraphrase is **true**.
